Your warm kindness made us fall even more in love with New York. Thank you so much. You’re truly the best pizza—and it was one of the best moments ever. 💛 A hundred stars!

author: Ellen Turner
review_text: Big portions, fresh ingredients, great value. I liked that they had impossible meat and friends liked their jerk chicken. I do wish I had read the review that said to get a bowl before our visit, the burrito is a two hander and will burst with the amount of food they put in it.

author: Jimmy Y
review_text: Ordered uber eats from here, paying full price for half the portions isn't fun. Can't recommend the delivery here.

author: Yvngumar
review_text: Couple things to say about this place. 1 its a pretty small place to dine in not much tables around as you can see in the video but plenty of space to move around. The menu is pretty wide as in there are a diverse amount of options to choose from which is good. It’s Mexican grill so the 2 main course are tacos and or burritos. There is also the option of the bowl which is plenty if you ask me but not as much as it would be in its counterpart hot peppers. Hot peppers and Guac time are kind of like the apple and Samsung companies in this situation. Both are competing within the same industry of Mexican grill restaurants and both have relatively the same options when it comes to choosing the ingredients. There are only a few slight differences like the portion sizes, sauces available, pricing, locations etc. I will not get into every one as I would be here forever but all you need to know is that compared to hot peppers this place is somewhat lacking. I paid $17 for a burrito bowl for half and half portions when the guy clearly charged me for double. I also told him to tell me when I was ordering something that would cost extra and he neglected to do that so communication is not a strong point in this place. Overall the atmosphere is clean and oriented and it does smell nice so I will give them that.

author: Conner Nevel
review_text: Fresh and tasty ingredients. However, do yourself a favor and get the bowl They’re not great at wrapping your burrito

author: Dana Curran
review_text: A great quiet place to get delicious food in generous portions. This is like what Chipotle used to be, but with better quality and not a massive corporate chain.

author: Jack Gray
review_text: Visited the restaurant for the first time today and everything was flawless. The guy that built my bowl was friendly, accommodating, and diligent. Everything was incredibly clean and the AC was working overtime, and while I didn’t dine in, the seating looked comfortable and ample, as far as the Chipotle-esque restaurant model goes. The bowl itself was a great value; it tasted great, was uniformly constructed, the ingredients were fresh, and it was extremely filling, which is a hard find around here these days. For $15 I can’t think of a better value in the neighborhood to be honest. I’m vegetarian/pescatarian so the impossible meat and fish options were clutch. I enjoyed this over Chipotle by a long shot, and am happy to have a quality alternative.

author: Kagu Kagus
review_text: Food is really good. Portions are fine only if you buy at the store. Used uber eats to get their food the other day.... bowl had such a small portion in it. For a moment i though driver ate some of it 😆 (he did not)

author: N. T
review_text: It’s SO GOOD but I had food poisoning from this place (burrito bowl)

author: Pete Deserto
review_text: The spicy cauliflower burrito bowl over lettuce is a delicious and refreshing meal on a hot summer day. The crispy cauliflower, combined with flavorful guacamole and mango salsa, creates a delightful explosion of taste. The freshness of the lettuce adds a nice crunch to each bite. Overall, it's a tasty option for those seeking a flavorful and healthy dish.

author: Zaryab .Z
review_text: Salad Bowl - Light yet filling, with a perfect mix of fresh veggies and flavorful dressings. A great choice for a healthier meal option.

author: Inshrah Siddiqui
review_text: Salad Bowl - The perfect light meal that’s still full of flavor. The fresh ingredients make it a refreshing option for any time of day.

author: Rameen Mansoor
review_text: Salad Bowl - A fresh option packed with crunchy greens and your choice of toppings. It’s light yet very flavorful.

author: Umair Saqib
review_text: Burrito Bowl That’s Just Right! Loaded with fresh toppings, flavorful protein, and a perfect balance of textures.

author: Dil ki bt
review_text: Loaded Nachos - These nachos are the perfect snack when you’re craving something cheesy and indulgent.

author: Omar Waqar
review_text: Great prices and portions. Lots of seating and clean. Close to the water. Much better than Chipotle

author: Nachiket Mehta
review_text: Angel - wow. Never experienced better service in NYC. Amazing burrito also. Highly highly recommended.

author: Yaniv Gheber
review_text: Very friendly and quick, great food! Great if you're hungry and need a perfect quick meal!

author: DREX Official
review_text: Went here for the grand opening and was 2nd in line; super friendly staff and customers lol; I had the jerk chicken and bought a bag of chips!

author: Melinda D
review_text: Delicious 😋, I recommend the mango salsa on your burrito bowl

author: Alisha
review_text: The flavors are fresh and vibrant, and the staff is super friendly

author: Anthony Nieves
review_text: Whoever thought of this place is a genius, a moderately small space but lots of choice, friendly staff, fast service, and an app that lets you order seamlessly and has Google pay as an option. 10/10 would recommend and the food is just the icing on the cake, amazing tender and seasoned boneless chicken with tasty, crispy fries, this is just an absolute unicorn of a place and you should try it! If the owner is looking at this, I would love to be a part of any advertising/ promotion because I enjoy this place so much!

author: B E
review_text: We ordered salads from Royal Greens and overall it was tasty just like other salad places in the area. There wasn’t a lot of each of the toppings added and they forgot the avocado which were paid extra for. They also don’t note which of the salad dressings have dairy and which do not. Overall the app works well, quick and easy ordering/pickup, and good promo for new customers. Customer service was also responsive to issue with missing avocado and credited the account. I’d give a half star extra for that. We’ll try again and see how it goes. Decent concept of being able to order different foods from one place to pickup.

author: DESMONT
review_text: Wonder Williamsburg is a fantastic spot with a unique concept! I especially want to highlight the salmon bowl—fresh, delicious, and perfectly balanced. Every detail of the dish reflects the high quality of the ingredients and great care for the customers. The atmosphere is cozy and modern, creating a welcoming vibe. It's definitely a place I want to return to and explore more of their exciting menu!

author: Emily Moenning
review_text: I got shrimp tacos from the Mexican brand. Flavors good, shrimp cooked nicely. Cold and stiff corn tortilla led to cracking and breaking. But it’s nice and thick. I feel like if they warmed up the tortilla I would be giving them a 5/5 stars. It’s nice in a pinch because you can choose different cuisine options and it’s right by the Trader Joe’s which is good for errands. I would come here if you’re starving and need something convenient but if you want tacos because you’re trying to have like a cute Mexican lunch you should just go to an actual taco place.

author: Dave
review_text: Oops all ghost kitchens!!!! Never seen worse reviews for a place on google ever. This place operates TONS of ghost kitchens on grubhub. Why? Because if they told you the food was coming from wonder, you would check the reviews and not eat there. Unfortunately, this is something you have to do now for any restaurant you don't recognize. It almost tricked me and I am pretty pissed about it. Go away.

author: Emily Porter
review_text: Love this place . Mya does an amazing job every time I order a meal. She’s very pleasant and professional. I appreciate her customer service.

author: Jimmy Tanico
review_text: Ordered the brisket and gotta say I was pleasantly surprised. I get the concept and was skeptical. Got the brisket home and I was genuinely impressed with the price and value. My daughter lives in Williamsburg and I am in the suburbs and I expected the typical Williamsburg price gouging. Honestly, I am writing this after buying the same brisket meal a second time. When you go back to a food establishment and order without looking at the menu - that's good food.

author: Vijay Kabaria
review_text: This might be my first review ever. I seriously hate this place. My whole heart hates it. I think it’s a cancer to new york city and williamsburg. it’s soulsess. it’s private equity for food. my biggest qualm, apart from the bad food is that their branding is wonder. hopeful. magical. and yet they’re so lifeless. they pretend to be serving all these bespoke restaurants— this is literally a ghost kitchen. they market so hard. i hate them so much. god this place sucks.

author: Nick Boyd
review_text: This place is really gross and not worth trying even if you get one of the coupons they offer. Nasty reheated meals premade in a commercial kitchen in NJ and heated up in a water bath or microwave for you. Completely cynical corporate restaurant concept that’s essentially a ghost kitchen masquerading behind marketing budgets and false claims of being a “food hall.” Terrible for small business, terrible for your taste buds. Skip it.

author: Faye Zheng
review_text: If you wanna some microwaved food, feel free to order here. Or you can just buy from trader joes and save you 80%

author: Lee Martin
review_text: I’ve yet to have a bad meal here or one I wouldn’t order again. Bobby flay steak NY strip was cooked and seared perfect. Tejas BBQ brisket a thing of beauty. Limesalt like an elevated chipotle, wish there was more guacamole in the side but all in all, the food is always ready for pickup very fast and food is fresh. Have been able to take advantage of the promo codes w friends and take food to the park it’s a life hack.

author: Jiahui Jiang
review_text: I mostly order their briskets which is a five star. Other things I tried there were mediocre. Ordering online then picking up later is super convenient

author: Simon P
review_text: Delicious food that you order online via the app for pickup in store. Service is usually good but can be a miss sometimes.

author: Rob Z.
review_text: Interesting concept, terrible execution. Much is lost in the transition from a restaurant to a central kitchen, with terrible food quality standards as well.

author: Erycka Ortiz
review_text: such a good experience and accesible. the food is fresh and taken care of.

author: Dan Barman
review_text: Beware, I’ve had real Di Fara’s many times, and this is not it. Food is fast and convenient but not good. My wife and I tried 4 different places through Wonder (including Di Fara’s), we had high hopes, but everything was subpar. The people working the counter are very nice

author: Ryan Huber
review_text: Poor quality food served at a premium price. Disrespectful to the consumer.

author: Clement Gomes
review_text: Amazing, amazing, amazing! Such an awesome concept to get a delish variety of food options and can be delivered right to your home!

author: Eric Lamy
review_text: The food was great the service was on point. Will go there again

author: Diego Cejas
review_text: Excellent! The food was delicious and the service was incredibly fast! Highly recommended. The menu is very varied!

author: Carin Rudich
review_text: Eyval is a must especially if you love Persian food. The restaurant is open and airy and is much bigger than you realize. There are three separate dining areas to it. There were 3 of us and we definitely over ordered but wanted to try different dishes. See the photos. We had some serious leftovers. The cocktails are unique in flavor and easy to drink. Our waiter was very sweet and thoroughly explained the dishes and guided us on what to order. The entire staff was very personable every time they came to the table, either to bring food or clear the table. Unbelievable flavors in these well curated dishes! Reservations required!!!

author: Kiariladyboss
review_text: One of the most delicious Persian dinner and food in NYC. They are usually booked 2 weeks in advance but people cancel all the time so keep checking for a spot to become available. The squash spread and the eggplant dish were out of this world🤯🤤 Loved the Persian cocktail too. Service was fast and staff very nice. Spot super recommended!

author: Robyn Lewis
review_text: Excellent everything. Really good food, nice wine, great service. Loved the octopus and squash dip in particular. I will be back and send others here. I wish I could have tried the whole menu! Just amazing. Also loved the radish etc salad!

author: Aylin A
review_text: This Persian fusion gem never misses. Every visit delivers incredible quality, from their must-have kashke bademjoon to the perfectly seasoned koobideh. Their seasonal additions—like the new mahi and kabab torsh—bring a bold, sour-leaning flavor that’s just as unforgettable. Reservations can be tricky at prime hours, but the first-come, first-served bar seating is a lifesaver. If you want consistently exceptional Persian fusion, this is the place

author: Sara Kazemi
review_text: I was visiting New York, and my friends had secured a reservation here weeks in advance — and I can see why! The vibes were immaculate — a perfect blend of modern and Persian aesthetics. The music, the staff, the atmosphere — everything was spot on. We ordered the Barbare bread with masto moosir, the octopus kebab, the kashkeh bademjoon, and the kebab — every single dish was incredible. The flavors were authentic yet elevated, enhancing traditional Persian spices beautifully. This was hands down one of the best Persian meals I’ve ever had outside of someone’s home. 10/10 — if you haven’t tried it yet, you need to. Absolutely amazing! I will deff be going back here when I come to New York again

author: Graham Parker
review_text: Utterly outstanding. One of my best meals of 2025. I was recommended to come here by my husband, who is a tad obsessed with it, and now I can see why! Nothing better than seeing a thriving spot take food, dishes, ingredients, service and buzz so seriously. The menu is varied and full of surprises, and not all dishes will work for all the pallettes at the table, and that is what makes it fun. You share everything and try lots of culinary ideas and see what sticks!

author: Massimo
review_text: We went to Eyval for dinner and found parking without much trouble. The place had a nice energy with a modern look and a comfortable crowd. The kitchen was fast and the food was excellent. The ghorme sabzi had deep flavor and tender meat. The tahdig was golden and crisp, and the kabob was juicy and well seasoned with saffron rice and grilled tomatoes. The servers, however, weren’t very attentive. Drinks sat empty for a while, and it took some effort to get their attention. For two people, the total was about $120, which felt fair for the quality. Overall, Eyval delivers top Persian food and a great vibe, but the service could be more engaged to match the kitchen’s pace.

author: Isabella Grandic
review_text: Maybe I got a bad apple, but this was some of the laziest, sloppiest service I’ve had… ever. Especially for a restaurant of this calibre. (Will elaborate) The food was good. Some of it was not good. The beef short ribs tasted were filled with what tasted like canned beans. Lamb ribs, which everyone seems to holler about, were not for me?? I couldn’t eat more than 1. A combination of the texture + the overpowering sauce. The bread is good but y’all it’s $6 bread. It should come with the dips. The yogurt dip was basic but good. The Brussels sprouts dip was good. Desserts were good! Only thing I would order again is the Wagyu kebab situation. That was yummy I think the play here is a lot a lot of dips. Maybe the fish / chicken is better than the red meat, it didn’t hit for me. The drinks. The Saffron martini tasted purely like moonshine, I got exactly zero saffron. Their coffee based cocktail I didn’t love (tasted cheap?). The cucumber mint one was alright and the mezcal pepercorn one was good. Draft beer was super whatever. However, our server was on a different planet, one where attention to detail doesn’t exist. She came up to us for the first time asking for dessert. I was like we’ll start with the meal first 😂. Ordered cocktails which took 30+ minutes to come. Then, when it came to ordering food, we asked for recs. She started just recommending something and then adding it to our bill. I had to stop her, ask her to please stop adding things to our list and let us choose lmao. “I will add one of those” should not be something the server says, unless it’s on the house! It took her 45+ minutes to return with a draft beer. When I asked for the dessert menu, she gave me the drink menu and returned 20 mins later asking what we wanted for dessert, to which I had to say, I don’t know because we didn’t have the menu! They also delivered the wrong bread and the wrong cocktail during our dinner A lot of people have loved this place and I fully went in hoping to join the club, but unfortunately this meal and experience fell quite short for me.

author: Reza Nia
review_text: We had been long waiting for the opportunity to try Eyval, and it turned out to be a delightful experience overall. The ambiance was warm and inviting, and the servers were incredibly friendly and attentive. The food was a mix of good and fantastic. The lamb ribs were absolutely out of this world. Chenjeh was also fantastic. For both dishes, I would happily give them more than five stars if I could. Koobideh was good, on the upper side of good, I would rate it 4.5 stars. Ghormeh sabzi and tahdig were both below my expectations, I gave them 4 stars. Overall, the restaurant experience was more of a 4.5 to 4, but I had to choose between 4 and 5 stars, it would definitely be 4. I will definitely return if it’s only for the lamb ribs!

author: Nima Azizpour
review_text: Eyval is by far the best Persian restaurant I have ever been to. The food is absolutely fantastic—each dish feels like a true work of art. Chef Ali is not only an incredibly talented chef but also a wonderful human being and a true artist when it comes to creating unforgettable flavors. The vibe of the restaurant is unmatched. Everyone who works there is so warm and kind—it feels like being welcomed into one big family where their only goal is to make every guest happy. The energy and atmosphere are just perfect. This place deserves a Michelin star without question. Everything is made fresh the same day, and you can truly taste that freshness in every single bite. If you’re looking for an unforgettable dining experience, Eyval is it.

author: Rebecca McCall
review_text: Worth the wait! The drinks, the decor, WOW. Highly recommend the Brussels sprouts. The saffron cream sauce this sit in is TO DIE. ❤️💚 Friends were out of town, so I went alone anyway and didn’t regret it.

author: Ali Bakhsh
review_text: Contemporary Persian food with a lot of great menu options executed at a higher level. Overall I enjoyed my dining experience here, there wasn’t really a standout dish that blew me away.

author: James On Al
review_text: I wish this place was good, but We couldn't find what we're looking for and Price that we paid absolutely does not match the quality we get from the food, Some dishes tasted really but others tasted like nothing , flavorless or flat. They did good job with adding spices to tahini and other sauces and dressings, but again not all dishes..... Waiter was not able focus or answer our all questions , They were just rushing, running.... Our experience was just okay, May be but may be can come back just for specific dishes hope they can keep their tastes good

author: Pamela A
review_text: This place is awesome! My family and I had the best meal. The menu is made for sharing. Every dish we ordered was the best I’ve had. The service was great. The team worked together seamlessly. We were not rushed. The dishes were brought out in a timely fashion. Our table was never devoid of food. The drinks were unique and delicious. The vibe was great!

author: Brittany Ng
review_text: Eyval was nothing short of fantastic! This was my first time trying Persian food and I was truly amazed by every dish we tried. The flavor combinations were unique and delicious, with the perfect mix of sweet and savory. We tried both the komaj bread and barbari bread, which had perfect textures of soft and fluffy. The citrus date salad was super refreshing and light with deep flavors from the dressing and dates, which was the perfect appetizer. We decided to try the lamb ribs, octopus kabob, and kabob koobideh as our entrees. The meat for all dishes were amazingly tender and flavorful, with the ribs falling right off the bone and the octopus perfectly chewy. The star of the shows in these dishes however, was the tomato butter that was served on top of the basmati rice in the kabob koobideh! It was so savory without being salty and wish there was more on the plate. I recommend all of these to share! The interior was simple but beautifully designed, creating a nice ambiance that takes you out of New York City. As you walk further in, you’re able to view the kitchen where chefs are carefully crafting each dish. The service was exceptional also! Our server was very attentive to our table, making sure dishes were cleared and plates were swapped out for an easy dining experience. I also mentioned it was my birthday and they served my dessert with candle, which was a very thoughtful gesture. Overall, this place was the perfect birthday dinner and glad I ventured out to try new food here! We are already thinking about our next visit to try more of their menu as I’m sure every dish will not disappoint.

author: Anja A.
review_text: This place is amazing! We went two times in a short period of time since we were thinking about their food and other dishes we haven't tried. Some of the must tries are: Barbari Bread, Yellow French Bean Borani, Citrus Date & Cabbage Salad, Lamb Ribs, Grilled Scallops, Eggplant.

author: Cameron Weeks
review_text: Good Persian spot in East Williamsburg with tough to get reservations. The bread and dips/sauces were probably our favorite items but everything was delicious. The kebab plate was also more plentiful than we were expecting and tasty.

author: Debarati
review_text: The food is SOOO good. This was supposed to be a stop during my trip but realized that our rehearsals for our NY performance clashed exactly will Eyval's opening hours. I was super sad so my husband decided to get me take out!! I am SO pleased. He got me photos of the food and the plating is so beautiful. I hope I get to visit NY again just so I can eat at Eyval again haha ..and perhaps next time in person! I got to try the lamb...I don't even know how they made it that good. I loved the dry pomegranates on top. The color is so beautiful too. Tried the salad & the roasted eggplant. Both very yummy. The cardamom chocolate cake was DIVINE!! 😍 Highly recommend!!!

author: Sue-Ann C
review_text: Eyval wants to be taken seriously as a dining experience, but someone forgot to plan for New York in winter. Let’s start with the absurd: there is nowhere to put a coat. No rack. No hooks. No designated space. Just guests awkwardly draping long winter coats over weak chair backs and laps like it’s a casual café in April. And if your coat is long, it’s now dragging on the wet floor from snow laden shoes in the dining room. I even asked the hostess (who asked the manager) where can I put my long coat and both had ZERO solutions; so, I ended up resting my faux fur coat on the edge of a planter off the ground. This is NYC— we are fashionable and winter isn’t a surprise! If you’re charging these prices and aiming for elevated dining, basic hospitality logistics matter. Service didn’t help. While very polite, our waiter messed up the order, he missed an item then gave incorrect information so we ended up with three very hefty rice bowls which imbalanced the meal. They also delivered a slice of chocolate cake for my birthday with a candle with no fanfare… no song, no “happy birthday,” no joy; it literally felt like a plop on the table. The cake wasn’t even good - tasted like it absorbed the smells of the fridge (they professionally removed that from our bill - thank you). And speaking of balance: serving a feta dip with no bread (and no proactive explanation or accompaniment) is just baffling. Dips require vehicles. This isn’t revolutionary dining—it’s basic sense. The frustrating part is that the food itself has moments of brilliance. The flavors are thoughtful, layered, and crafted with care. Very rich. Which makes the execution issues even more glaring. Eyval isn’t missing the mark because of ambition—it’s falling short because of avoidable oversights. In a city overflowing with restaurants that understand both food and fundamentals, Eyval needs to decide what it wants to be: a memorable dining experience or a beautiful concept undone by preventable mistakes. Right now, it’s hovering uncomfortably in between—coat in hand. It’s not worth the reservation scarcity.

author: Frank Garcia
review_text: I was wowed by my experience at Ey-vál. This has been one of the best Persian food I have had, they certainly ey-vál which is a Farsi(Persian) word that adds positive emphasis to an idea. I’m surprised they are not in the Michelin guide but I’m sure they will make it sooner than later. The service was top notch. Super friendly and professional, fairly fast, knowledgeable about the menu and attentive. Ambiance was dark, enigmatic, hip, I liked it a lot. The food, what we came for, was beyond delicious. We started with the Mast o Musir and I gotta admit I have had great ones before and thought it would be hard to beat, but this one goes to the top of the list now. So so creamy, with shallots cut at the perfect size and acidity balanced out. I continued with a salad( can’t remember its name) and while this was not a truly Persian dish, I loved the modern approach and all the flavors they accomplished on this dish. It was my second favorite dish after the mast o musir. The lamb ribs were a solid dish. The sauce had the perfect sweetness/acidity as well as spiciness and the barberry on top complemented so sell. The two kabobs were nicely done but my favorite was the koobideh. This is a personal preference as I’m more into koodideh than steak kabob. I understand the chenjeh is more premium, but it is just my preference. All in all, the 2 kabobs were 5 out 5 stars. Tahdig which is one of my favorite Persian dishes and a really simple dish, was perfection in a single bite. That sauce they had the rice on, it was spot on. They made it also so good looking. I loved it. You can’t leave a Persian restaurant without having Persian ice cream. However, to be honest it didn’t do it for me. There were a few flaws : typical Persian ice cream sandwich is with crispy and thin waffles, this one was with a soggy bread, also the ice cream was not as creamy as it should be. The ice cream sandwich was subpar compared to the high quality of the food I had. All in all, looking forward to my next time at Ey-vál. Please open a location in Miami :)

author: Riccardo
review_text: Buzzy/noisey atmosphere at the entrance, good host and reception with drinks at the bar before table was ready. Waiters not really alert, they messed up with my order, still smiley at least. The pizza is very good/authentic Italian, average price 20 dollars each, but the service is very slow(and I mean it). Can’t say I loved the dessert as I left most of the pancake. Will still be definitely back as the it’s probably best pizza in Brooklyn.

author: Kevin Shapiro
review_text: Kitchen cool Brooklyn vibe. Indoor and outside seating. 2 bars. The one we were at you could get food from, but every time you went back up for anything such as a drink or anything like that you had to stand on an enormously long line and wait quite a while, which wasn't great. The meatballs were very good, and the regular and Margherita pies were very tasty. Crust was soft, not crispy and thin.

author: Beyase Warton
review_text: My friend and I wanted to stop by a place to get something to eat before we went back home to the city and this was recommended to us! They make really good daiquiris and their pizza is delicious! The staff was nice and the whole vibe of the place "outside" was so cool!

author: William Kim
review_text: Really good neopolitan style pizza. The dough is so good. One of my favorites. Fresh ingredients. I got the Famous Original and Bee Sting. Both had a little spicy kick to it, nothing crazy. Honey on bee sting was perfect combo to spice and soppressata.

author: Andrew Schneider
review_text: Amazing pizza joint, perhaps the best I've had in Brooklyn. Dive atmosphere. Great wine list. Service from Lauren was amazing.

author: Pat Lisi
review_text: Well I’ll start with saying I’ve never been so sure I was about to be robbed as I was when our cab driver took us into this industrial area which was pitch black as it was night time. When the car stopped and there was nothing around I was sure it was my time to go !! However the cab driver pointed to a red light over a small vestibule and said “that’s it” was beyond relieved to know we were still gonna make it !! As we had no reso we had to wait two and a half hours for a table as the place was packed. The pizzaiolos were very friendly and talked to us about everything pizza and more. I asked some questions about the oven as it didn’t look like any I ever saw live or when I shop for my own and then they explained it was basically home made on the spot and that’s just amazing and very cool .. especially because they’re churning out NYC’s best pizza. Very vibey atmosphere , very friendly staff … incredible pizza. 🍕 10/10

author: R Juliza
review_text: Honorary mention to Luis who worked diligently and gracefully even when something wasn’t up to par Luis ensured to fix it right there and then no hesitation no attitude or mal intent. Such a kind soul made me feel like I was right where I belonged. Thanks Luis. S/o kitchen staff also food is yummmieeee

author: Rovik Robert
review_text: Very good pizza in a vibey Brooklyn space that has lots of character. Decent selections of beers and wine to pair as well.

author: Ti Na
review_text: Don’t judge a book by its cover. From the outside, you question if you’ve come to the right place but don’t let that fool you,the food is great! Highly recommend a reservation. When you walk in, you’ll be greeted by the pizza oven and staff. Atmosphere is cozy, low light with candles on the table. We had a salad to start along with olives and meatballs. All were good and large enough to share. The pizza is Neapolitan style. Crust is very good, soft with the slightest crunch and char. Sauce is good and toppings of sausage and meatballs are flavorful. Staff were attentive and very nice. They’ll box up your left overs for you too. Will return.

author: Tera Nakata
review_text: A solid, tasty pizza. Slightly pricey. Got the Waingro and Bee Sting. A bit out of my way to get here but would recommend if you're in the neighborhood.

author: Susy “REALTOR” Velazquez
review_text: Loved it! The atmosphere at Roberta’s is rustic and inviting, creating the perfect setting for a great meal. We tried four different pizzas, and each one was delicious. The flavors were well-balanced, the crust was perfect, and everything tasted fresh. Highly recommend for anyone looking for good pizza in Brooklyn!

author: stephen shustock
review_text: Wow just amazing pizza and one of the best I’ve ever eaten! The bee sting was amazing and so was their famous original. The atmosphere is eclectic and definitely funky and strange but it’s an amazing experience and the food is so good I can eat this every day and not get tired of it!!!

author: Benito Camesta
review_text: Such a cool vibe, it's a bar with amazing pizza. I got the bee sting based on all the reviews and it doesn't disappoint. The dough is so light, there is a spicy to it but all the flavors compliment each other so well.

author: Amanda Lynch-Smith
review_text: I’ve been to Roberta’s a bunch of times and it never disappoints, but I want to give a special shoutout to the staff who always make the experience memorable. I ordered the pizza with ricotta, white sauce, and added mushrooms (delicious), and even though there was a delay with it coming out, Simone went above and beyond. She was so attentive, kind, and genuinely fun to talk to — she really made me feel special. Also huge thanks to Blair, who has helped me and my boyfriend out on Valentine’s Day and other visits to snag a table. Between the incredible food and the amazing team, Roberta’s is one of those places you always want to come back to.

author: Jose Miguel
review_text: Funky spot with an amazing vibe and seriously good pizza! The Bee Sting was hands down my favorite – spicy, sweet, perfectly balanced. We also tried the Lil Stinky, and it was packed with flavor. Surprisingly, the salad blew me away. I’m not even a salad person, but this one was super flavorful and creative – a total standout. The place has that refined grit – it doesn’t look fancy, but everything’s done with care and intention. That contrast between raw and elevated? It just works. Definitely coming back!!!

author: Eric Lam
review_text: Had a grown-up pizza party birthday dinner here. I haven't been back here for years, and everything's as good as I remembered. We sat in the room in the back. I really liked the shipping container decor. Service was pretty good. Food came out quickly. Although we had a small issue with two of the pastas being way too salty, the rest of the food was excellent. The English Pea caramelle was nice. I particularly enjoyed their Margherita and Lupetto pizzas. I would also recommend their maitake mushrooms as well.

author: Diana Arday
review_text: The pizza here was 10/10. Really nice and freshly made. Only issue was they had 1 working restroom so the queue was long but other than that, a really nice place to eat and catch up with friends.

author: Adrien Qi
review_text: fire vibes inside but ordered takeout. satisfying chewy crust and very good flavors. texture couldve been better but we got takeout and ate after 20-15 min of walking

author: S Yoon
review_text: I'd describe the pies here as modern Neapolitan. These have a bit more structure than traditional Neapolitan pies. That said, the ingredients are fun and the vibe is cool. It's been a few years, but I'd definitely go back.

author: Ruben
review_text: I live in the neighborhood I’ve been here 3x and every time the staff was in a hurry and a bit rude (being annoyed when they didn’t hear something or not wanting to explain something on the menu etc). I understand that these simple customer service things don’t come naturally to people that don’t get paid a living wage, but Roberta’s is very group-oriented with tables (I don’t think they let you order just a slice 🤷🏻‍♂️) and that’s just the kind of thing that happens when dining as a group so I think the staff should be patient when someone has a question. So far I haven’t felt any kindness from the servers so I won’t be returning anytime soon. It’s also way overpriced, there’s way better pizza and cheaper cocktails right nearby. Go to Moondog for cocktails and to Starrlight for a full-size pizza

author: Patrick Zajac
review_text: First time trying Ethiopian food and I’m glad it was at Bunna Cafe because this place was stellar! Absolutely loved the ambiance, service, and most importantly the food. They start you off with a free plate of popcorn to snack on while you wait for your food which was so fun. Also, I happened to be in during their weekend Bunna Coffee Ceremony so I had a complimentary cup of the Bunna. It was very strong, spiced, and rich, with a prominent ginger undertone. Adding in the brown sugar cubes opened up the flavor so much. Delicious! I tried the Lentil Sambusas which were super crispy. The filling inside was fine but adding on that cilantro lime sauce really tied it all together! There was a subtle spice too that I enjoyed. For my main I went with the Beyaynetu Meal which was the 5 scoop option. I kinda wanted to go for the 7 scoop Feast to try more things but I’m glad I didn’t because the 5 scoop was very sizable for one person! I tried the Enguday Tibs, Shiro, Misis Wot, Yater Kik Alicha, and the seasonal option which was an Eggplant and Walnut Deberjan. WOW!!! Everything was so insanely flavorful and worked well with each other. I think my two favorites were the Shiro and the Yater Kik Alicha. Soooooo so so good I could eat a whole bowl of just those.

author: jen k
review_text: This was my first Ethiopian cuisine experience and I loved that they don't give you utensils for the full effect! The food isnt really a looker if you're not into pureed food, but the taste was delightful! Highly recommend and for any vegans or vegetarians craving some hearty food. I have gone 2 times now and they are just as good! The interaction (bread) they have is tangy and slightly sour.

author: Maitri Bhandari
review_text: From the moment I stepped into Bunna Cafe, I was completely charmed. Tucked away in Brooklyn, this all-vegan Ethiopian spot radiates warmth and culture, and an inviting, communal vibe. They even host an authentic Ethiopian coffee ceremony in the evenings, which adds to the immersive feel. The staff was wonderful, warm, welcoming, and happy to answer questions about the menu and traditions. We kicked off our meal with Kategna, a crispy, toasty injera snack paired with Daata, a spicy side sauce that delivered just the right amount of heat. Simple, but incredibly satisfying. Next came the highlight: the Feast. It’s a platter of injera topped with vibrant scoops of various stews and vegetables. Each one was distinct, bursting with flavors. The crimini mushrooms were earthy and umami-rich, the lentils hearty and beautifully spiced, and the collard greens brought a fresh, slightly tangy contrast. The Shiro, a spiced chickpea stew, was deeply comforting and packed with flavors. Honestly, it was impossible to pick a favorite. Every bite felt thoughtful, nourishing, and made to be shared. I sipped on refreshing Hibiscus tea throughout the meal, which was the perfect complement to the bold, warming flavors. Bunna Cafe is a celebration of Ethiopian cuisine and culture. Fun, flavorful, communal, and deeply satisfying. I’ll definitely be coming back.

author: Ellen Levitt
review_text: I have gone here occasionally over the past several years and the food is always wonderful. I went today for lunch because it's Sigd and I wanted vegan food. The kale was amazing. The others really tasty too.

author: Siena WD
review_text: Unfortunate that I finally found a go-to/favorite Ethiopian place in the city a few weeks before going home for the summer. It took some time to get here but I was very committed to procrastinating my homework, and if you're an ethiopian restaurant offering me a vegetarian combo there's really no limit to how far I'll travel for that. I got the feast for two (though I am only one. Next night dinner. It's called being smart) and apparently they offer this to go in a pizza box which is very smart and fun however I worried it would be clunky for the subway so instead I got a million containers of greatness. My photographs as always are of dubious quality, but rest assured the food was not. The injera, thank god again, was sour, I hate when it's bland but this was far from it, the perfect vessel for all of everything. I don't know all the names of the dishes but I loved everything I ate. The mushrooms stood out, I love gomen, the split peas and red lentils were doing their thing, something was spicy and idk what it was but it was ASTOUNDING I say really the whole meal I was just thrilled with so I had it again that weekend and loved it just as much. When I picked up my orders both times! The person working was friendly and warm and unbelievably kind, I'll have to dine in next time because I imagine the service is top notch. I'm going to enjoy my summer away from the easy coast but I will say, this spot will be on my mind and I'm looking forward to being reunited with the greatness that is Bunna Cafe.

author: N. Sergew
review_text: Phenomenal place! Ver tasty vegan Ethiopian dishes, along with delicious coffee and spicy tea. Wonderful and attentive service. Went for brunch and the live DJ just enhanced the whole experience so much! Highly recommend!

author: Christopher Kong
review_text: I had some business in the area and want something to eat and thought about Bunna! I had no reservations and had about a 20-30 minute wait on a Saturday night. I am now convinced this is the BEST Ethiopian place for great vegetarian food! The place was packed even as late as I arrived. Very warm and accommodating staff. The food was so on point! We ordered drinks as well and just as amazing as the food! It is a little out of my normal area but I will surely go out of my way to get back here again.

author: Neha Rege
review_text: Bunna Cafe was my first Ethiopian food experience, and it instantly made me fall in love with the cuisine. The food was rich and flavorful, the ambience felt warm and authentic, and the service was friendly and attentive. A great spot for anyone trying Ethiopian food for the first time or looking for an authentic Ethiopian experience in Brooklyn.

author: Nicole Smith
review_text: Come here for brunch!!! The food was absolutely bonkers! Portions were also great for the price, two of us split three dishes and both had leftovers to take. Both of us really enjoyed our teas as well. The service was quick and kind and the vibes were wonderful with the music in the background. Highly recommend!

author: Jasmin
review_text: Best Ethiopian food in the city (that I know of). Flavorful and fully vegan!, value for money, and service is friendly and quick. Ambience is casual and cozy. Good playlist, on weekends they sometimes even have live music. Fri, Sat, and Sun they have the coffee ceremony at 5pm and serve free Ethiopian coffee, which is also delicious! Have been here for dinner multiple times and weekend brunch (different menu).

author: Laura
review_text: My mother and I had a lovely dinner at Bunna Cafe. The staff was attentive, kind, and courteous. Every bite of their food was a delight and the wine and tea were also delicious. The lighting and atmosphere were soothing. We were visiting the neighborhood for the day and would love to dine there again if we're in the area.

author: C. Tapia
review_text: I came where with my parents who are VERY picky eaters but they loved the food! The flavors are fantastic. The colorful portions are beautiful. We had a handful of the lentil sambusas, the feast for two, their Ethiopian version of a Bellini (YUM) and the baklava for dessert. A delicious meal with hearty portions. We left feeling satisfied but not overly stuffed. And everything is so healthy and simple ingredients

author: Gary Gao
review_text: Great vegan food with wide variety and also good coffee. Personally I liked the samosas the most

author: Shako Liu
review_text: I’m a visual person and I love how colorful the foods are. But more than just visuals, the taste is supreme! I come here a lot when I crave for something delicious and healthy. The staff is always kind and friendly. This restaurant is a neighborhood gem!

author: Kelly He
review_text: first time having ethiopian food! i think it tasted good and felt good quality but 1. didnt realize its vegetarian lol thats on me 2. the tables/chairs were weird heights so it was a little uncomfy and the live music on wednesdays was wayy too loud :// we got the feast for 2 and feast for 3 for 5 of us. it was so big (see photos for size comparison) and the shai tea was p good too! overall the food is good. id imagine youd love it if you were vegetarian and/or love ethiopian food but im not convinced its for me quite yet

author: Olivia Celice
review_text: I observed the consistency that builds Bunna Cafe's reputation. Worker attention was truly exceptional! The portions here are notably generous. The food works well, but the atmosphere truly excels. Hope this place impresses you too.

author: Queeny Qiu
review_text: Loved the ambiance of the restaurant! Lots of seating and great service. Didn’t know what to expect for vegan Ethiopian food but was not disappointed. The flavors were amazing and really enjoyed the roti that we got with our main dishes. Brunch prices were reasonable and portions were generous! Highly recommend!

author: Kiariladyboss
review_text: First time trying Ethiopian food 🇪🇹 and i went with a friend for my b.day. Enjoyed the experience to eat on the same plate. We ordered the feast for 2 (even though that’s food for at least 3 people😂) for $49 + a couple of appetizer and mango juice (freshly squeezed) that is served with pomegranade syrup (if i am not mistaken). On a mission to try all the vegan spots in NYC

author: Mo Da Prophet
review_text: First time trying Ethiopian food? Go here! Food: Authentic and delicious food. Feast for 2 was perfect amount for 2 people. Each dish had its own distinct flavor and you can explore different flavor combos. Food came super fast as well. Service: Staff is friendly. They more less leave you alone. Perfect, if you’re looking to eat alone and not be bothered.

author: Floz Panseri
review_text: Bunna is always the best. On point from the time you walk in trough the ambience till the first bite. I LOVE BUNNA. One of the best vegan worldwide

author: rachel
review_text: Ayat, can only be described as a euphoric dining experience. This restaurant has quickly become a favorite among friends in the city. The atmosphere is incomparable, cozy enough for conversation but busy enough to hear the laughter and joy around you. The food is indescribable, beautifully seasoned with unforgettable flavor. The staff is also incredibly kind, and very thoughtful in their service. Some menu highlights were the halloumi watermelon salad (truly life changing), the Pistachio Paradise Pizza, and the Chicken Shawarma. All dishes were amazing, but these were each unforgettable. Ayat is the spot to go if you want a unique and outstanding experience in a homey environment with beautiful ambiance. This is a must-try restaurant, I’ll be taking every visitor I have!

author: ana
review_text: I had such a wonderful experience at Ayat! The food was absolutely delicious — full of flavor, fresh, and beautifully presented. The atmosphere was cozy and welcoming, perfect for both a casual night out or a special dinner. Our server, Yulisa, made the experience even better. She was so attentive, kind, and knowledgeable about the menu. She made great recommendations and checked in at just the right moments without ever feeling rushed. You can tell she really cares about her guests having a great time. I’ll definitely be coming back soon — everything from the service to the food was amazing!

author: Benjamin Freeberg
review_text: Pretty nice experience overall. Very warm and welcoming inside. The staff is a little standoffish they didn't make any conversation which was off-putting but my friend and I had a good time together. BYOB is nice too. I'll definitely come back to try more of the food.

author: Rachel Cheung
review_text: I’m very picky in a way that I know enough about ingredients and cooking techniques so believe me when I give them a rare 5 stars from me. Top quality ingredients, hummus was silky smooth you can taste every subtle flavors because they use good chickpeas, spice, and olive oil. Then the mixed grilled platter with lamb chop/ kebab were outstanding. Juice clean fat and well cooked. Desserts are pretty but too sweet in my opinion. Wonderful service our Ecuadorian waiter was excellent!

author: Kenia Mendez
review_text: The service from Lissette was excellent – very kind and attentive the whole time. The food was delicious and different, full of flavor and beautifully served. I loved the pita bread, so soft and fresh. I tried the Hibiscus Margarita (the purple drink with mint) and it was amazing, super refreshing and unique. My dish was the Mixed Platter, a perfect combination of chicken, lamb, yellow rice, and veggies – everything was spectacular! Definitely an experience worth repeating. 💚

author: Deval Shah
review_text: Amazing food . Everything we tried ( and we tried many vegetarian items) was very high quality ingredient wise and also well cooked. This place is now my #1 for Mediterranean style food. great addition to the community. Thank you for your effort! The pita, fried halloumi, muhamarra, kanafe, eggplant, labneh, vegan platter were all amazing.

author: MOE JARADAT
review_text: What an unfortunate situation — this restaurant was on my bucket list. Unfortunately, the experience was spoiled by the less-than-professional behavior of Natalia. That said, the restaurant itself tells a wonderful story, backed by an amazing menu. The atmosphere truly reflects and supports the spirit of the people of the land. Special thanks to Susan, who made things better for us. Constructive note: Please avoid serving Arabic coffee in a glass tea cup — you know the culture better than that

author: Amirah Randolph
review_text: I absolutely loved dining here. The cuisine was delectable. The staff were lovely, especially Suzan. The live music tied everything together. This was the perfect birthday experience. I would definitely recommend everyone come and visit.

author: Sunny Patel
review_text: Place is gorgeous! Food was alright. Service was alright as well. Don’t get the spicy chicken kebabs - subpar at best! The chicken sumac dish was good - very mild taste thou. I’d go back to try other dishes. Didn’t love what I had. The pita and hummus was great thou!

author: Jacob Moss
review_text: Honestly everything was phenomenal. We got the Mezze Filistini, the Makloubeh platter, the Watermelon Haloumi salad, roasted cauliflower, and the Baklava Sundae. All the dips in the Mezze were stunning—best tabouleh I’ve ever had. And a huge shoutout to that watermelon haloumi salad, it was revelatory. Like, I didn’t know food could taste like that. Really nice atmosphere, overlooking the park with open concept, and also it was a Saturday and they had live music!

author: Shonalya Fonseka
review_text: Amazing food, amazing atmosphere truly one of the best restaurants in the city. Staff was so kind and helpful especially Chris, the art was so beautiful and you’ll see only smiles on everyone’s face. The energy was great definitely excited to come back again

author: Jack Michalski
review_text: Went for a birthday dinner. Service was accommodating and friendly. It was BYOB and we brought a bottle of wine and there was no corking fee. Food was good across the board. Lots of vegetarian/vegan options. We got: baba ghanoush (smokey), fried halloumi, vegan platter (too many good things to list but especially liked the zahir and wara dawali), and the grilled salmon salad. Reasonable prices. Will definitely come back again

author: Ss Kk
review_text: We celebrated our friend’s birthday here and had such an amazing time! The food was delicious, the drinks were on point, and the place has such a great vibe. Definitely recommend checking it out. Special shoutout to our waitress Suzan she was the sweetest and made the night even better. Thank you for the great service!

author: Nick Richards
review_text: This spot is always a 10/10. Informed and educated waiters and staff, delicious food with huge portions, and it’s BYOB! They also have different atmospheres, outside, inside, and downstairs - each with their own vibe.

author: Sapphira Bella
review_text: We came here for a friend’s birthday dinner a few weeks ago and got the downstairs seating section. The place was jam packed and very busy. It’s BYOB so we brought our own wine, tequila, etc. The vibe was cute and homey. We had the appetizers to start with of za’atar, labneh, hummus, etc. The bread was not great quality and the dips were OK. We tried the vegetable platter, a lamb kebab and a chicken kebab. Everything came with pilaf and salad. Overall the food was very OK. It was decent, lacked seasoning and some of it was not cooked well. The service was very good and they accommodated our large party but the food was underwhelming.

author: Astrid
review_text: Ayat, where to begin? Sometimes a place draws you in because of its reputation. Ayat was one of those places. Seated on a Sunday, I came in with moderate expectations of a thorough menu dedicated to showcasing Palestinian cuisine. I was not disappointed. From the zaatar to the olives in olive oil, to the heaping mounds of sizzling chicken shawarma, Ayat is a place that beats expectations. Nearly too much food to eat, so go with friends that like to share and indulge to your hearts desire. Food is the star, but the service is excellent too, and the ambience is deeply inviting. Palestinian to its core - what a beautiful place!

author: Kee Diamond
review_text: I went to a Palestinian restaurant in New York for the first time. As expected from its popularity, everything was delicious. I was very satisfied with both the atmosphere and the service. I definitely want to go again

author: Daniella Favila
review_text: Good was amazing! Liz, our server, was the most kind and tentative server! The food was very warm and comforting, we loved the BYOB aspect and the people were amazing and kind! They knew how to explain the dishes well and were personable.

author: Arin Dutta
review_text: Bushwick branch of the Ayat Palestinian restaurant network in the NYC region. Was pretty crowded already on an early Friday evening. The location also opens a small patio facing the Maria Hernandez Park so you may want to target that. Food: - at this location at least, not that amazing. Pita is flaky and thin, and nicely flavored. You can have better in the 5 boroughs area, sure. - hummus: my dinner companion is bit of an expert and according to her (I concur), it was heavy on the tahini and lacked bite (traditional Palestinian hummus can be a bit creamier than other Levantine recipes so this may well be true to design). It is nicely presented in a traditional earthenware bowl, as is most of the food. - Shawarma platter : we got the mixed grill version. The rice and toppings were generous and the meat was flavored though not excessively - Fattoush: nice and lemony, with a good helping of fried pita chips - We asked for kibbeh, and only after 15 minutes of waiting, were told that they had none! Overall: not the best nor the worst Palestinian food you’ll have in the region. Service is a bit klutzy. Ordering tip: the shawarma platter is pretty large. Can satisfy two people (with a starter like hummus) if you are not ravenous. Photo of mixed shawarma platter, hummus, and fattoush attached

author: Denissa Gonzalez
review_text: We received complimentary pita bread fresh out of the oven such a nice touch! The hummus was delicious as an appetizer, and the lentil soup might honestly be the best I’ve ever had. I also really appreciated that they don’t go heavy on the salt, but my cucumber and tomato salad ended up way under seasoned it definitely needed a pinch more. As for the service, our waitress seemed kind but very out of it. She looked tired and sad, like her body was present but her mind was elsewhere. She kept forgetting things, tripped over her feet a few times, and even dropped the dressing. Service felt a bit off, but I genuinely hope she’s okay. It left me a little concerned.

author: Anja A.
review_text: I did enjoy the food at Hellbender, but the service could have been better. We were among the first guests seated, yet it still took about 5–8 minutes for our server to notice us and bring water. The portion size of aguachile is quite small, considering the price. The Brussels sprouts lacked flavor. On the positive side, the empanada was amazing, as were the mushroom tacos and fried cheese.

author: Jordan Napolitano
review_text: Came here for brunch on a Sunday, had a reservation. Sat at the bar for a drink before we went to our table. Drinks were really good we had a few each, service was great. We ordered a few different things, the bloody Maria mignonette with the oysters was tasty and a little spicy. The pork tacos were incredible and of course we got the masa pancakes which were delicious but so filling. The jello of the day was a Concord grape jello with peanut butter drizzle and a homemade whipped cream which was really really good. Would love to come back here. And the bathrooms are huge!

author: Christopher Blair
review_text: Ordered about 9 or 10 dishes here and all were incredibly delicious. Dishes are ordered to share. Also tried a margarita and a bloody maria, very well made cocktails. Highly recommend, worth a trip to Ridgewood just to visit the excellent Mexican restaurant

author: Rob C
review_text: To start off I wanted to love this place. My wife and I love trying Mexican restaurants. Very friendly staff and service was great. Now for the food thats another story. We ordered the fried oaxacan cheese and it was a little greasy but good. We also ordered the pork tacos I have to say the pork itself was bland but what they top the tacos with was delicious. For mains I ordered the chilaquiles which was not good. It was cold and had no flavor like it needed salt or something. My wife ordered the enfrijoladas and again was just bland missing those wonderful Mexican flavors. Overall it was a big disappointment food wise. Something me and my wife were excited about.

author: Stephanie Logan
review_text: Very tasty. The chips and guacamole were crunchy and fresh. The Oaxacan cheese was perfection. I also really enjoyed the specialty drink. It contained a liqueur made by monks. The drink was a great compliment to the meal

author: wallace dos santos
review_text: Easily five stars, maybe even six 👀🤌 seriously delicious food. Like seriously, this is game changing. My friend and I started with Chamoy Pear dish, which was absolutely mouth-watering and zesty. Then we got the Baby Gem salad, which was an interesting New Age twist on a Caesar. THEN, omg, we got the lamb shoulder with some tortillas on the side. DAMN! That went crazy…. And the sauce… omfg. Soo fricking good. No notes, just so delicious. Service was excellent & we sat outside. Would have loved to have gone inside or tried dessert. There were so many other dishes on the menu that seemed really interesting as well, and unique flavor combos. Apparently there’s a real stuffed cheetah in there (allegedly). Can’t wait to go again!

author: Franco Scardino
review_text: Great food and drinks! The mushroom tacos and hamachi appetizers were a real standout. The cheese empanada was reminiscent of a calzone, but more delicate and refined. The crispy lamb is a must and bursting with flavor.

author: Jim Blair
review_text: We ordered several small plates / appetizers for brunch and shared them. Literally every one was delicious. In total we had about 9 or ten different plates, from guac and chips to mega thick cut bacon (pictured) apple pear salad to enfrijoladas and more. Probably the best meal so far of our visit to Brooklyn. Don’t miss it!

author: Leandra Edelson
review_text: First off, the churros are INCREDIBLE and I can’t say this enough. The whipped cream is salted a tad, which perfectly balances out the peach compote and sweetness of the churros. I love a salted whipped cream and have never found a restaurant to do it. 10/10. we got a seafood platter special app which was truly fantastic. The steak was also great especially with the charred peppers, we got tortillas on the side which was perfect. Mushroom tacos are a must and so is the fried Oaxaca cheese !!!! Really great experience and super friendly staff

author: Daniel
review_text: Delicious brunch with a Mexican twist. The masa pancake in particular was unreal. The fried crispy edges mixed with the soft and moist center. Perfect blend of sweet and savory with the syrup, butter, and spices on top. 10/10

author: Es Thompson
review_text: Amazing!! Go there!! The service was sooo good. The hostess was so nice and friendly. Staff kept checking on us all night and giving us etas on the food which was appreciated but unnecessary because everything came out faster than expected. Waitress was very helpful and gave great feedback on choices. Food was out of this world. We order so much so we could share and there was not a single thing that missed. My friend had to covertly unbutton her pants lol. Everything was soooo flavorful and well balanced and thoughtful. Im not a huge fan of tacos but I ate these right up. Comes with 2 which are about 2 bites each. You really have to finish them there because they didnt look like they would hold up well going home. Steak basically melted in my mouth. Ive never had such a well made steak. The waitress suggested medium rare but I asked for medium and it was perfect. I struggled to finish it but again new that it wouldnt reheat well at home. My friend got the lamb shoulder and that was also delicious , has a nice kick and that was even better the next day reheated. The watermelon....I could eat 100 pieces of it. I had to tell myself not to lick the plate. The churros with blueberry compote.... oh man! I had no idea that blueberries had so much game. Absolutely delicious, not overly sweet, paired so well with the churros and the cream. I was so sad when I reached the bottom of the bowl....churros, I miss you everyday. Only complaint is had out of the whole experience was that it was a bit noisy...it got better as people left for the night. This is also a me thing so I won't judge the restaurant for this lol but I hate bathrooms with black toilets. And just an FYI for anyone with a shellfish allergy, they informed me that they use the same fryer for everything so the lamb shoulder is a caution since it uses the same fryer as the shrimp.

author: Raul Bussot
review_text: I’m a big fan of Rollo’s so it’s no surprise that Hellbender is just as impressive. I would return to enjoy all of the dishes I had and there were several we didn’t get to try. The smashed cucumbers, fish tacos and crispy lamb were outstanding. I look forward to retuning and trying the rest of the menu!

author: Jelvis Ferreira
review_text: Hellbender just served me the best pancakes I’ve had in NYC—hands down. The heirloom masa pancakes here aren’t just good, they’re game-changers: perfect texture, flavors that complement each other beautifully, and nothing overpowering. Every bite felt balanced and memorable, to the point where Clinton St. is officially dethroned as my previous pancake champion. I’m already counting the days until we come back. We also shared the skirt steak and the coffee tres leches cake—both phenomenal. The steak was cooked perfectly, paired with flavorful potatoes and a rich butter topping, and the tres leches was indulgent without being too sweet. Between the three dishes, my wife and I left full and completely satisfied. The staff here deserves a special mention. They were knowledgeable, professional, and had excellent communication with the kitchen, even advising on what to avoid for dietary restrictions. That level of attentiveness made the experience even better. Hellbender delivers on flavor, balance, and hospitality—absolutely worth a spot at the top of your NYC dining list.

author: Kary Sartan
review_text: Oh my God, what can I say about this place??? too many things.. from the Agua Chile to the tacos to the lamb shank to the mole I am speechless. ALSO THOSE DAMN PANCAKES ::: JEEEEEEEEZ. Food heaven! This place has an epic menu with epic flavors. It’s a great space. I love it for our neighborhood.

author: Alison Pouw
review_text: same owners as radio bakery. went for brunch and got the egg tostada. i would love to go back and try the pancake. the egg tostada was good but needed a bit more flavor/salt - a bit oily. it was good but not incredible. the grapefruit juice was incredible if you’re into that. cute decor inside too.

author: Lauren Smith
review_text: Dinner was a lack luster. The best thing to order are the mushroom tacos, the carrots in the tostadas could be softer and use less sauce. Don’t order the chicken Milanese or the steak. Both came out burnT. Brussels sprouts also very burnt. You really shouldn’t be eating burnt food, that causes cancer. bill was close to 200$ which is underwhelming for a sub par experience

author: Thomas Lo
review_text: The gulf prawns were delicious, perfectly cooked and seasoned. A gem of a restaurant in Queens.

author: Dolma Yankey
review_text: Quick (not rushed) service, delicious food, chill atmosphere! The fried Oaxaca cheese was scrumptious, the lamb taco was so good (didn’t even realize I was eating lamb- nice and crispy, and not gamey at all), scrambled egg tostada delish- seemed like Chinese dish inspired due to the chili-oil, and the masa pancakes 😋 - top notch. The pancakes were super moist, hot, with a good amount of butter and maple syrup, just the perfect dish to end our brunch! The portions are on the smaller side. But super happy with our first-time experience. Will definitely come back ;)

author: Ryan Wenzel
review_text: Hellbender is a standout spot with fantastic food and a great vibe. We tried the fried cheese, aguachile, mushroom tacos, and pork ribs al pastor—every dish was memorable, and I only wish we had room to explore more of the menu. As someone who loves meat and takes tacos seriously, I was especially blown away by the mushroom tacos—absolutely a must-try. Can’t wait to come back!

author: Sangeeta Joshi
review_text: Some restaurants leave a lasting impression with their food and service. Hellbender is definitely one for me. Fried oaxacan cheese and crushed cucumbers set the bar high and the dishes that followed got better and even better. Pork carnitas tacos, chilaquiles very satisfying but the highlight of this brunch was soft scrambled egg tostada and heirloom masa pancake. The tostadas with the chilli oil and sesame had a Chinese dish vibe, so flavourful! The pancakes with a generous slice of butter…something very special, unique taste for a pancake. First bite tasted almost like gulab jamun, an Indian dessert. Service was excellent! Hope to visit soon.

author: Марта Пляцок
review_text: at first glance a nice clean new facility. but it was a deep disappointment. the food is not tasty, very salty. the pizza was not pizza but pita bread and cheese and leftover chicken. the chicken was heavily seasoned with vinegar and salt. everything was terrible, except for the cashier who served me. it was my first and last visit. all the food had to be thrown into the trash. the food does not match the photos on the poster. as terrible as possible, and not cheap. the food stinks of fat and vinegar. I spent $56 on it and threw it in the trash. Thank you.

author: Bavdun Umar
review_text: I love this place! That’s so hard to find good Halal food in United States and I am so happy that in 5 min from me I have this beautiful place. The fries are so starry and crispy ! Chicken delicious 🤤 thank you so much for good service and asking How Is my day today! I live Muslim Culture and Ethics that’s how people on Earth should treat each other! Mash Allah Halal Tamaq yehmen dégenler razi bolidu. I made a Combo for $ 13 and get so good substantial food. They work late. Deliver is also available.

author: Tiffany Love
review_text: I ordered food from here via Uber Eats. I got an order of fried Oreos, Small waffle fries and 10piece honey bbq wings (5flats & 5 drum). The fried Oreos 10/10. The fries 10/10, the wings 7.5/10. The drums tasted amazing but the flats tasted a bit old. Their ranch is also 10/10, it tasted like wing stop ranch. I will definitely order again though but maybe earlier in the day. (Forgot to take a pic of the fried Oreos)

author: Madison
review_text: I was super excited to get some good wings. So I ordered a 10 piece, honey barbecue wings, a 5 piece, lemon pepper, and a pineapple mango smoothie. I opened my wings, and they looked delicious.But then I realized a wing was missing in my 10 piece honey barbecue. I was very heartbroken since they were pretty pricey, but they were still delicious. I also had to wait 25 minutes for my order.

author: Yolanda Jones
review_text: I try to like this place because it's halal but WOW oh mighty never again. I tried this place several times & can't recall as it was some time ago but I won't forget my experience this time. Almost everything on the menu is fried, which is no problem as we know it's not healthy but for every bite I take, it literally is going to give me hypernatremia. Not a pinch or a dash of salt but a literal handful. I feel my blood pressure rising. I could not finish after 4 bites of the garlic flatbread. I shouldn't be dying for water after each bite of food from whatever im eating. What a waste of money as I threw the food out. What's even sadder is that I decided to break my fast by eating from here. Service was good though. I just don't recommend as almost every review is in agreeance that the food is SALTY

author: Sergio Morales
review_text: Chicken sandwiches were really good. Idc about the “quality of service” so it gets a 5/5.

author: Carlos Morales
review_text: so i tried these before and my order was sent via ubereats wrong when they just opened. today i went in person the guy at the register was nice, great service and they got my order right(still wasnt too familar with the menu might i add) but out of all places ive ordered lemon pepper wings this seemed to be the worst. usually in other spots the u can taste the lemon pepper in each bite. it just tasted bland and i threw out half my order. the fries were good tho but for a wing spot i would expect better wings. kinda regret giving this place a second chance. i did however love the drink. tasted different in a good way and not too sugary. but unfortunately im not returning for wings ever again.

author: Stephen Lewis
review_text: Not gonna lie, this is more a 4.1/5 and it’s also weighted for the neighborhood, but this place is a solid go to for me, especially when I’m feeling really lazy. Low expectations are key here , but I honestly can’t complain much. The one time I ordered celery and carrots they were a bit out of date, but that’s more on me than anything. The 10 boneless wing and French fries combo all day baby

author: Sander Hicks
review_text: Hey, this is a really great place positive place to eat! Wow the $8.99 five boneless wings and waffle fries combo special is a great value. The chicken is solid breast meat, not composite nugget meat. Inside, friendly atmosphere with music videos. Julio always remembers me and remembers I don’t like to use plastic bags. Nice guy, great food!

author: Renee Davis
review_text: okay so this place has really good boneless wings. crispy. but they literally get the order wrong every time. they handed me bone in wing and this is a COMMON occurrence i saw the reviews and they do this so often i thought it was just a fluke but literally happened to me. i would be so annoyed if i got home and didn’t notice. but luckily i did before i left. also they take like 20 mins to cook 5 boneless wings not normal. also they charged me for the boneless wings and it’s basically the same price to add fries as a combo but they won’t tell you that… bc they want you to spend money. kinda shitty would give service one star but it’s not like they cussed me out they were nice just kinda slow at everything

author: Jeremy
review_text: Stop by here from time to time to grab buffalo wings and fries, which taste great. A lot of reviews are bombing the place, but if you get the tossed medium buffalo wings with regular fries, im telling you, you can't go wrong. It's more so up to you whether the price is right. It could go for being a dollar or two less but still would buy as is.

author: Ray Dalto
review_text: I must say I'm very impressed with this place, It's very clean , owner is very welcoming, and service is fast , wings were great they have a variety of different flavors, my favorite was the Chile, you guys they even have rice on the menu. First time I ever purchased food from here but I must say I'm returning. For my brothers in Blue Highly recommend.

author: Sophia Rivera
review_text: I’m horrified with the customer service here. The French fries for one are plain they don’t even carry salt and pepper which would be nice since Dipping sauce isn’t Free…I’ve never heard of a food business that doesn’t offer at least one or two dipping sauce complimentary.I’m talking 10 DRY LEMON PEPPER WINGS and nothing but ketchup to dip it in…gross.I’ll also add that it costs $1.00 for sauce a size of a dollar coin.ridiculous.Then we have the front desk worker who looks like he rather be laying back chilling at his house than to Be doing his job.This guy for one BARELY spoke English.For two Got my smoothie Order wrong three times even though we pointed out the image of which drink we Wanted.THREE he was eating a meal like he was on his lunch break when we walked in and FOUR took OVER 30 minutes to make our SMOOTHIE in the first place! This man took his sweet time with EVERYTHING and Had to be reminded that we ordered a drink and never received it.THE GAG Was when he finally did make it after the 30mins went by IT TOOK UNDER 5 minutes to make!!!! So why were we waiting a HALF AN HOUR?THE AMOUNT OF CUSTOMERS IN THE SHOP IS NOT AN EXCUSE BECAUSE THEY DIDNT START COMING IN UNTIL A FEW MINS AFTER WE ORDERED AND THE GUY LITERALLY DIDNT HAVE TO DO ANYTHING BUT TAKE THE ORDERS.Horrible Horrible Horrible! will not be coming back.

author: Linh Nguyen
review_text: I've only ordered for pick-up, and it's been good so far. Their spicy chicken sandos always hit the spot.

author: Dangst 55
review_text: They have a varieties of sauces for the wings, which actually taste pretty great but the fries weren’t good at all they were hard. I recommend strictly for the wings only.

author: SINCLAIR SINCLAIR -
review_text: They burnt my wings I tried them before Too much obay seasoning i had throw some away . Today my wings are burnt . Great service But the food i had i could've went to wendys . Good day 🥴

author: James Sailor
review_text: Not a bad place. Food is decent wings had a good taste. They followed instructions if im in the area again will deff come again

author: Rafael Rivera
review_text: Stole my money after showing receipt. They sent order to different location. When they said they remake food had me sitting there 30 minutes waiting and did nothing. Never again. Stole my money with no refund direct through website.

author: web master
review_text: The lady behind the counter is very, very rude. After a very long wait time, the food did not make up for the rud3 attitude. Very bad experience and a waste of money. I don't recommend this place.

author: Ramon Alomar
review_text: Food was very good not Greasy and not salty they had napkins and forks the service was good

author: Kevin Ajemian
review_text: The food is absolutely stellar. One of my favorite German restaurants. From the authentic layout to the service. All of it is top notch. I recommend this German restaurant to anyone. One of the last bastions of an old German establishment. My favorite is the pork shank or beef rib with horseradish sauce on the Friday specials. 👏👏

author: Peter Gruber
review_text: Great German food. With an old world atmosphere. The workers are wonderful and explain anything on the menu including what type of beer they serve. The food is excellent. Try the Jaeger schnitzel. And for desert the apple strudel is a good choice.

author: Jonathan O'Buckley
review_text: There are so many different dishes, you gotta come here multiple visits to try it all. Can't go wrong with getting Snitzel and a nice cold beer. Tried Käsespätzle for the first time, and that was a great appetizer. If anything, be ready to take a doggie bag home because of their big portions. Always leaving full and happy.

author: Don Miller
review_text: I haven’t been there in years but stopped in recently for a late lunch to satisfy a craving for a taste of the old country, and a good German beer. Food, service and atmosphere was very good. Das jaegerschnitzle ist Wunderbar 😋🍺🇩🇪

author: Jonathan Harris
review_text: Solid, although not outstanding German food. Quite busy on a Saturday afternoon. Cozy restaurant with an Oktoberfest feel. The Jägerschnitzel was excellent. I've eaten better Sauerbraten. Kids menu was sufficient. Was nice to have a Hofbrau beer to wash everything down. Good service considering how busy the restaurant was.

author: Mary Naughton
review_text: I was back in the neighborhood and able to stop into Zum Stammtisch. My father used to take us and other family members here as frequently as we could. We often would see Aurora. Tonight, in memory of Dad, Mom and I came in for dinner. The waitress was lovely. I ordered rieslingschnitzel, which is veal schnitzel in a light riesling and mushroom gravy, I had the creamed spinach with it and the schnitzel was served over deliciously crisp home fries. Mom got the jägerschnitzel with the traditional darker mushroom gravy and also the creamed spinach. I wanted something a little different for a beverage so I got the coffee that has brandy in it. In the past, I’ve also had their goulash soup, which is a favorite for all and their potato pancakes. I’m so sorry the pork store has closed next door, I enjoyed going there as well. A few helpful hints for those who have yet to try this neighborhood icon, they take cash and card, they’re closed on Mondays, parking is hard to come by so get here earlier and prepare accordingly. Also, they close at 10pm however, their kitchen closes at 9pm, so to get a meal, you’ll need to be in before then.

author: Stephen Hatzis
review_text: This is literally better food than in Germany. 🇩🇪 my go to spot in NYC. Great authentic food and beers. Great atmosphere.

author: Zachary Feigman
review_text: One of the best restaurants I've been to in a long time. It reminds me of my grandmother's and mother's cooking so to me it was very authentic. The staff were excellent. Our waitress was very nice and fun. I think the prices are very reasonable. You have to try the steak tartar and the herring in cream sauce. For entree, I tried all my friends dishes and everything was excellent, especially the jagarschnitzel. Unfortunately the Pork Knuckle was out, or I would have ordered that. One of my highest ratings in a long time. Go here immediately.

author: Elisabeth Ivanov
review_text: Zum Stammtisch is a great spot. The food’s hearty and full of flavor — the schnitzel and sausages were excellent. Big portions and cold beer make it even better. The place has a warm, old-school vibe and friendly service. Feels like a classic neighborhood spot. I’ll definitely be back.

author: Łukasz Kuźniar
review_text: Good food, atmospheric decor. One star for the totally hopeless service.
