Now let’s get to the food😋😋 Wow oh wow is the best way to describe things.. I purchased a omelette which came with potatoes small portion of fresh fruit and I did a side of French toast which seemed to be a hit. And boy oh boy I’m glade I did it was A-M-A-Z-I-N-G ( highly recommend). My guest ordered Sweet Chili wings which were out of this world👏🏾👏🏾 so good I ordered some to go for later.. The classic margarita pizza (individual brick oven style) was also another amazing choice. Honestly our food was Divine!! Upon looking at the people around us their food choices seemed to be as well! After finishing our meal there was no regrets coming to this hidden gem. Besides the spacing inside, and possibly having to wait a few extra minutes to get a table, (food we’ll worth the wait) left us feeling the need to definitely come back to enjoy more authentic dishes.. 8.5/10 * I didn’t see where to tip on app, ( hey maybe I missed it ) but there is a tip jar at the very front cash register, in which they all split!

author: P M
review_text: A true 5 star review. I could ramble all day about how great this place is but if you’re reading this just go. You won’t be disappointed.

author: Jessica Campos TV
review_text: I'm on vacation in Boston and I loved this place. The food is great and the staff is very friendly. I'll be back soon!

author: Naj Barrett
review_text: How did I miss this place? Stopped in for brunch and we were all very happy with our orders, French toast tasted like a delicious Cinnabon, eggs full of flavor and thick pieces of bacon. I also had a fruity mimosa, in a nice lively atmosphere. Our server and everyone working there was awesome!

author: Melissa Gomez
review_text: We popped in for breakfast and it was so amazing! Highly recommend.

author: Alex Grossomanides
review_text: Absolute trash restaurant, should be shut down. Waited 30 minutes for a raw burger that cost $18. My wife's salad was bagged romaine lettuce on a plate.

author: Sonja Gomez
review_text: Food was amazing and the blueberry martini was the best I've ever had. That's also coming from 2 people who don't really drink we could barely finish one between the 2 of us. Atmosphere is great and it was very clean well kept restaurant 👍🏾

author: Ron Roche
review_text: Enjoyed a quiet lunch with my wife. The style and ambiance of The Joint is just what you'd expect in the new JP. Very warm and inviting yet high tech with QR code menus and payments. We both ordered the crispy chicken sandwich, mine with the chipotle sauce and hers without. I highly recommend the sauce. It added just a bit of a bite without overpowering the perfectly prepared chicken. The seasoned fries rounded out the plate perfectly. Service was quick and friendly while not being intrusive.

author: Kaytie Owens-Liston
review_text: We came for breakfast for the first time and were SO happy. The food combines the diner feel with a modern presentation. Highly recommend the combos so you can enjoy their pancakes (or waffles!) and all of the egg/bacon/potatoes. Mimosas are phenomenal - actually taste like there is sparkling wine and not just orange juice. Prices are absolutely reasonable given the quality of the food, drinks, atmosphere, and service. Highly recommend and this will become a regular spot for us!

author: Janet Depaz
review_text: May 2025, The joint has a new menu. See pictures attached. This place is a local gem! I enjoy eating there both during the week after work and on weekends with the family. The staff is always friendly and attentive, the food is really good (love the tacos, pizza, and wings), the cocktails are very tasty, they have specials every day, and at breakfast time the place is always packed. Parking off the street, music always playing!

author: Hope Pettengill
review_text: My sister originally had sent me a video of her trying a burger from this restaurant (I was so jealous it looked legit insane ) and then she brought us back with our family for Father’s Day. We were sat down with great service, it was rlly peaceful in there (we went during the day). Perfect place to grab lunch with family, friends or even a date. Half of us got the joint burger which speaks for itself. Just a rlly great burger. Regular burger with caramelized onions and joint sauce. I mean you can’t go wrong at all. We also got the chicken avocado club. Rlly filling and something where you just feel content after eating. Rlly good as well. Each item comes with fries that are some of the best fries I’ve had, rlly hot which is the most important for my fam and I. Great crisp as well. The owner, came up to my family and checked in with us and everyone who was sitting down at the establishment. He is a class act. Rlly down to earth, personal and great guy/ owner. Came back after a couple of minutes and gave us this fried ice cream dish, with fresh fruit, cinnamon and powdered sugar. Legit insane. Was gone in 3 min. I love this place so much. Pls go if you are considering you will not regret. I know we will be back soon that’s for sure 🔥🔥

author: Jim Tarwater
review_text: Welcoming environment and extremely friendly staff! Makes me wish I lived nearby. I had the Margherita pizza and my wife had the cheeseburger with fries. All delicious! We will definitely come back here when in town!!

author: Ceciliana Betancourt
review_text: Luis and his boss were both amazing!!! The food, drinks, and desserts were amazing as well!!! The drinks definitely do not disappoint! I've had an espresso martini, a passionfruit mojito, and a blueberry martini, and I loved them all. Shout out the bartender making them 🙌🏼 .. nice, chill place. Will definitely visit again soon!

author: Brooks Reeves
review_text: So the vibe is charming and inviting. I ordered the French Toast combo as I wanted a sample. I was disappointed that the meal came on one plate, which forced me to eat my eggs and potatoes first as I didn’t want to mix the sweetness of the syrup with those savory components. The bacon, while tasty, was limp. Eggs were quite good, but it’s over easy, not rocket science. Potatoes were decent though the serving size was paltry especially when you consider the price. I do not have a huge sweet tooth, and I can’t remember the last time I had French Toast, but I will say: it was great. Pillowy and with a strong cinnamon flavor. So pros: great French toast, and tasty food all the way round. Nice atmosphere. Cons: Way overpriced for what you get, and you don’t get much for that price. While the food was tasty I can get that meal, and more of it for close to half that price at countless diners around Boston. I just don’t think it was special enough to justify the price point.

author: Dara Behjat
review_text: Definitely worth the hype. The food is exceptional. Pizza Bianca with the tomato relish is delicious bite and the bread is so perfect, the pepperoni pizza with hot honey is probably the only thing we ate that you can skip but it's still really good, clams and guanciale is cooked to perfection and the sauce is addicting, the bucatini with chilli anchovy butter is one of my favorite dishes I've had, perfect chew and flavor. The sausage cavatelli was a delicious change of pace again a perfect cook on the pasta, finally the taleggio signature dish, absolutely delicious, if you're going with a group I'd probably get it as a shared plate because it is so so rich. Service was also stellar

author: Alexander
review_text: Finally was able to snag reservation that worked after a few weeks of trying to corral people together. The restaurant itself was great. I thought it was a little too dark but overall had a great ambiance and cute, subdued aesthetic. The music and general noise was also at a comfortable level, a nice touch which many restaurants get wrong. The service was also great. Very attentive and helpful for guiding us through the popular items, specials, and personal favorites. As a hungry group of three first-timers, we ordered 4 pastas, 2 desserts, a pizza bianca and sauce, and a slice of pizza. This amount ended up being right for leaving satiated without overly stuffed. The pizza pianca, like breadsticks, and pizza slice, like a "granny slice," was surprising light and really enjoyable. If you like crispy new york style this pizza won't scratch the itch but for lovers of flatbreads this is exceptional. The stracciatella dip was so good (the tomato relish was incredible!) as was the hot honey and pepperoni topping combination. We skipped the starters and went straight for the pastas. We split the taleggio cappelletti and each ordered our own: a seasonal butternut squash filled pasta, bucatini with anchovy chili butter, and rigatoni amatriciana. The pasta itself was outstanding. I love pasta with a bit of bite and this delivered. I thought the dishes could have all been a bit more flavourful. The popular cappelletti are little pockets of molten taleggio, a slightly funky cow's milk cheese and one of the favorites. I also really liked the rigatoni amatriciana. It was a much more tomato-ey sauce than I am used to for amatriciana and I really enjoyed it. The butternut squash raviolis were well done and bursting with sweetness. And the bucatini had all the umami from the anchovies and roe without being too fishy. Everything was good but they all lacked anything extra to be particularly special. I thought each dish could have used one more strong flavour to make the dish a bit more interesting. I had extremely high expectations due to the hype and hassle to make a reservation so that could have led to me being a bit underwhelmed. We finished off the meal with the tiramisu and panna cotta. Both were delicious, my favorite was the panna cotta. Overall, extremely good pasta and pizza and would love to return but for me, not sure I think its worth the hassle of planning a multiple weeks in advance.

author: Ivan Ang
review_text: We waited 2 months to get a reservation at this legendary Italian spot in the middle of Jamaica Plain. It wasn't worth the 2 month wait. I must add that our server was FANTASTIC. She was kind, attentive and immensely knowledgeable about the wines and menu. We just needed the food to be ½ as brilliant as she was. The bread sticks (Pizza Bianca) were good and the cheesy dip was worth the wait. The pizzas and pastas however, were painfully mid at best. We ordered the Cacio e Pepe, which is a Secret item available only upon request. When it came, the sauce was breaking apart and the dish was a little dull and lack a cheesy punch. We loved the Cheesecake but the Pina Colada and Tiramisu was boring. I feel the 2 month wait probably worked against the restaurant — after such a long wait, I think we expected way too much and it certainly did not meet expectations.

author: Carley Lemay
review_text: UNREAL. Every time I go to Tonino it’s a 10/10 experience. The food is absolutely incredible...easily the best Italian in Boston, and their specials never miss. The entire staff is warm, professional, and so attentive. Special shoutout to the lovely Taylor, who always makes the experience even better. I recently had my birthday dinner there, and the staff went above and beyond to accommodate multiple dietary restrictions and food allergies. Every single one of my friends left raving about the meal and is already trying to book a reservation to go back. I seriously can’t recommend them enough!

author: Chris Eng
review_text: Incredibly good in all respects. We've loved every dish across multiple visits. If for some crazy reason you're only ordering one pasta, pick the bucatini with chili anchovy butter and bottarga. Save room for the tiramisu, which is made using amaro (Meletti I believe), dark chocolate, and sea salt -- this combo balances out what in most other restaurants would be a cloyingly sweet dessert.

author: Hesam Azimi
review_text: Tonino has been one of the hardest reservations to snag in Boston, so our expectations were sky-high—and it did not disappoint. The restaurant itself is tiny, warm, and inviting, with carefully chosen art and soft lighting that create a charming, intimate vibe, and kind staff with amazing service. From start to finish, everything we had lived up to the hype. We started with both salads on the menu: the Trevisano and the Tomato. The Trevisano was tangy in the best way, while the Tomato Salad was even more impressive—fresh, vibrant, and beautifully balanced with stone fruit, tomatoes, and Fresno peppers. For mains, we tried the Pepperoni and Honey pizza, along with three pastas: Lumache with mushrooms, Cappelletti, and Bucatini with chili-anchovy butter. The pizza slice is served in two pieces, made on house-made focaccia, giving it a texture reminiscent of an elevated, crunchier Sicilian style. The sauce was beautifully balanced and paired perfectly with the spicy-sweet combination of hot honey and pepperoni. The Cappelletti was the star of the night—rich, cheesy, and elevated by a touch of aged balsamic that cut through perfectly. The Bucatini came in a very close second. Despite not usually loving anchovies, we were blown away by how harmoniously the flavors came together, with the chili butter adding heat and the breadcrumbs providing a satisfying crunch. The Lumache, while good, felt a little one-note compared to the others. Desserts were just as impressive. The ricotta cheesecake was incredibly fluffy and light, and while the panna cotta could have been a bit firmer in texture, the flavor was outstanding. The fennel and Snapdragon apple on top made for a delightful finishing touch. P.S , don’t sleep on the amazing tea selection they have, we tried the Yuzu genmaicha tea and it was delicious! Tonino might just be the best Italian restaurant in Boston right now, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see it earn Michelin recognition this November. We’ll absolutely be back—if we can manage to get another reservation!

author: Eric Johnson
review_text: Tonino Italian Restaurant is exceptional. I’ve been here twice now, and both visits were outstanding. The food is exquisite and prepared with real care. The standout dish for me is the balsamic tortellini, perfectly balanced, rich, and genuinely memorable. The atmosphere is warm, the service is thoughtful, and everything on the menu feels elevated. Easily one of the best Italian spots in the area. Highly recommend.

author: Cami Tussie
review_text: Had an incredible experience here - lived up to the hype based off the cappelletti alone. It is a MUST, I’ve never had a pasta experience like it before. The pizza Bianca is not a pizza, beware, it’s hot delicious bread. The ricotta and eggplant caponata we ordered with the pizza Bianca highly recommend. The tomato salad and mushroom pasta (lumache) were good, but not standouts. The tagliolini aglio olio pomodoro we wouldn’t get again (still delicious, but there’s better on the menu). Tiramisu is a MUST. Best I’ve ever had. Incredible and kind service!! Worth the stress to get a reservation

author: Sabina Shorey
review_text: Amazing restaurant experience! Everything I've had has been great and left wanting to come back. The waitress went above and beyond helping us with wine and aperitif picks. Small restaurant, can be hard to get a reservation but definitely worth it.

author: Andrew Levenson
review_text: Tonino was a gem! Delicious food and wonderful service. I enjoyed the pasta, Pizza Bianca and tiramisu. I will say, though, try Via Cannuci nearby. Less hype, but IMO it’s equally delicious and much easier to get into. Leave extra time to find parking!

author: Noyonika Parulekar
review_text: The pepperoni pizza slice with hot honey: nothing special. The bread was crispy and delicious, but the toppings were underwhelming. The sauce was perfectly tangy, but there wasn't enough of it, or the cheese. I also wish the pizza had come out more hot. Servers are very attentive here. I did notice that a lot of people with reservations were being asked to wait for a while to be seated. The small space is definitely the issue. Mushroom pasta - the mushrooms were meaty, pasta perfectly cooked, parsley was fresh and aromatic, and contrary to popular opinion, the portion size perfect (not sure if it was just this dish). However, it was a little saltier than I liked. I will say, it's nothing to write home about. Cocktail - I got the Bergamot Blush and it was delicious, strong, not too sweet, and very citrus forward. Overall, I think the food here is unnecessarily overpriced. While I would not come back here for the food, I might return for a cocktail in 3 years when I can finally get another reservation.

author: Varada K
review_text: Most incredible meal at Tonino. Went on a Sunday night for a birthday dinner and was absolutely blown away by the most incredible food. We started with the Pizza Biana woth ricotta and hot honey which was so smooth and creamy. Would definitely recommend everyone to try. Actually ended up getting more bread since the dip was so delicious . We also got the Margherita and eggplant and ricotta pizza slice which was so flavorful . The Lumache mushrooms pasta and the Taleggio Capelliti was like a taste of heaven. It absolutely melts in the mouth! Was so lucky to finally get reservations and so thankful to our amazing server for making it such a special night !

author: Dave
review_text: Went with the wife for a date night. Reserved a table just in case because we saw how popular this place is and it doesn't disappoint in that regard, especially with the small yet cosy feel inside. I had done some research on the menu before we arrived, so although we knew what we wanted we were open to hearing recommendations from our server because this was our first time dining at Tonino. These recommendations would not be ignored, as coming in, we knew we would order a pizza bianca but didn't know which. However, as we told our server we wanted the "small" that consisted of mortadella, pecorino, and house pickles, our server knew that we should try the ricotta and hot honey with the pizza bianca. That recommendation did not disappoint as the sweetness of the honey and the creaminess of the ricotta paired perfectly with the crispy and crunchy, yet airy bread of the pizza bianca. Shortly after, the mortadella, pecorino, and house pickles arrived on a platter. Now the mortadella had a nice aftertaste and pecorino cheese is always great, but their house pickles were easily the best pickles I have had in my life, hands down, not even close. In the end my wife ordered the bucatini and I ordered the rigatoni. The pastas themselves on both dishes were clearly handmade as labors of love to the customer. I do want to preface my thought on my main dish by saying that am not too cultured in terms of palatte or food exploration. That being said my rigatoni dish's sauce and topping of guancile I believe it was, was a bit too rich for me. But if that is the only complaint I can find about this establishment, then so be it. My wife (a slightly more travelled diner) told me that her pasta and the culmination of the mouth feel, flavor profile, and freshness made her believe this is a top 5 dish she has had in her life. If you are ever in the southern part of Boston and want AMAZING italian food, stop no further than Tonino.

author: Jimmy Zhu
review_text: Perhaps the snowfall toward the end of our meal added to the magic of Tonino, but even on an ordinary night, this place would still be exceptional. On my first visit, I turned to Yelp for guidance and settled on the most popular dish—the Cappelletti. We each ordered it, no hesitation, and it absolutely blew us away. It was rich, comforting, and exactly what we were craving. The ambiance at Tonino was cozy, dim, and lively. Our table by the window felt slightly cramped, but it only added to the charm of the experience, making for a meal that was both intimate and memorable. We also tried the Pizza Bianco, which, despite its name, isn’t actually pizza but rather bread served with dip. Unable to decide, we took our waitress’s suggestion and opted for a sampler of all three. If I went back, I’d go straight for the hot honey or the eggplant caponata—both were standout choices. The clams were tasty but not the highlight of the meal. For dessert, we ordered one of each: the tiramisu, panna cotta, and ricotta cheesecake. If I had to rank them, the cheesecake took the top spot, followed by the panna cotta, with the tiramisu coming in last. If I find myself back in Boston, I’d return to Tonino in a heartbeat.

author: Trinity D
review_text: I had a disappointing experience dining in here for an anniversary. It started with a 30 minute wait when we had a reservation for 8pm (it happens, but that is a long time and we were starving). The place is very small so seating is tight and you are very close to nearby tables. The service was good and friendly once we were sat. It is the mains that are really lacking. The bucatini was basically flavorless, just tasted a little spicy but not actually seasoned (noodles were a great texture). The cavatelli with Italian sausage was so heavy on the lemon I couldn't taste anything else; I could only take a few bites of this one. The lumache with mushroom and the taleggio were good but nothing special for the price tag. The pizza (tried the hot honey and pepperoni) was disappointing after having the pizza bianca; there was barely any hot honey and the sauce lacked flavor. There were a few exceptions: the pizza bianca with ricotta and hot honey is a 10/10, delicious. The tiramisu dessert is also good, even though I don't usually like tiramisu. The cheesecake was not really a cheesecake; it was more like whipped cream frosting on a biscoff crust (we did enjoy it, just don't order it thinking you're getting a typical cheesecake). I am just very underwhelmed and disappointed, as there were great reviews and reservations booked months out, and it's not cheap - plus they charge a 5% "kitchen appreciation fee" with a note that basically reads like "we don't pay our back of house staff enough so we're charging 5% extra," which I find a little tasteless. Maybe the chefs were having an off day, but I won't be back for dine in and I wouldn't recommend it. But I will go back for takeout for that pizza bianca, they have me there. The three stars are for the friendly staff and the pizza bianca.

author: Beth Anderson
review_text: 10/10 no notes. My only complaint is how hard it is to get a table here. I’ve never had a bad bite of food here, the cocktails are delicious. The service is impeccable and they always help me choose the perfect wine. The panna cotta with apples should not have worked.. but I practically licked the bowl and thought about the intensity of the flavors all the way home. You will find me hovering over my computer at noon desperately attempting to book my next reservation

author: Manasi Datar
review_text: Tonino is a little gem in the heart of Jamaica Plain. They have a small and simple menu, but you can't go wrong with it all the pizzas are delicious. Noteworthy pastas include the buccatini, cavatelli, rigatoni, and cappareli. They usually also have a seasonal pasta (for us it was a corn pasta) and it was sooo tasty. They also have a superb cheesecake on the menu. You must try it. We love this little place, and our hack is to go there either early or late on a weekday. Their bar seating is given to walk-ins and IMO the best seating in the house - it's almost a chef's table. Highly recommend this place; you won't be disappointed.

author: Katy Urda
review_text: An easy 5 stars. We’ve been here twice now and can’t believe that the second visit exceeded the high expectations set by our first. Everything we ordered was genuinely standout. Best Caesar salad we’ve ever had! Just go.

author: Jea Kim
review_text: The rumors were true. Best Italian restaurant in Boston. Finally made my way here this past Saturday night. As expected, the reservation were extremely hard to get. When we arrived, a long line had already formed by the entrance, and it turns out the buzz wasn’t unwarranted - two bar seats are set aside for walk-ins, but with no waitlist in place, it’s first-come, first-served. Tonino’s menu didn’t follow the traditional Italian playbook. No veal chops, meatballs, or even crispy calamari. Aside from a few seafood dishes like the clams and the anchovies, there weren’t a lot of protein options. Here, it was all about the simple dishes - pasta and pizza. The focus on the pasta’s texture and balance of flavors was especially memorable, and overall, it felt like Italian cuisine distilled to its purest, most artful form where very bite felt like a celebration of simplicity done exceptionally well. Favorite Dishes: Pizza Bianca with Ricotta & Hot Honey, Bucatini, Panna Cotta Every dish we tried was amazing. From the first few dishes, my favorite was the Pizza Bianca. Essentially a deconstructed pizza, it came with warm, pillowy bread meant for spreading with your choice of dip. What made it even better was its versatility. We ended up using the last few pieces to soak up the clam juice from Counterneck Clams. The basil they used had a strong fragrance which played beautifully with the briny clam flavors. The Cappelletti, the most popular pasta on the menu, didn’t quite live up to the hype for me. The aged balsamic added a pleasant sweetness on the finish, but the Taleggio cheese felt a bit too overpowering. Wasn’t a bad dish by any means, but the balanced was tipped into overly salty territory. Among the other pastas, our favorite was the bucatini. Instead of relying on a heavy sauce, this dish let two powerhouse ingredients - anchovy chili butter and bottarga (cured fish roe pouch) - do all the work. In other words, a pasta that didn’t lean on the usual tangy seafood flavors but instead delivered a beautifully restrained, deeply umami rich experience. Most importantly, the Panna Cotta with basil sugar & apples. Easily the best dessert I’ve had in Boston. No description could truly do it justice, but here’s my best attempt: the panna cotta itself was exquisitely creamy and impossibly smooth, the kind that melts on your tongue. The finely diced apples added a crisp, refreshing contrast, while the basil sugar brought a delicate, herbaceous lift that made each bite effortlessly balanced. A masterpiece in simplicity and an absolute must-try.

author: Zach Oschin
review_text: Best restaurant we’ve been to in Boston. Food was excellent. Restaurant is small and romantic and service is great. Highly recommend if you can get a reservation.

author: Philip Yazbak
review_text: Fantastic food! A massive menu and quick service. I got the Nashville chicken sandwich and my friends got some pizza and the pulled pork sandwich. The food was incredible and the price was fair! All in all you can't go wrong stopping here!!

author: Humble Servings
review_text: 1st time actually coming here & they deliver! I decided to call in & do a pick up today & glad I did! The staff on phone & in person are the best! The food all looks is great! Pizza hit the spot! Love their fries! Will be back for their homemade cookies 🍪 We really need more good customer service like this place, 10/10 Highly Recommend 😋

author: Kathy Yu
review_text: WOW! First time here and I love it so much. The slices are large and the crust is thin. The toppings have fresh ingredients, and there's so much variety in the slices you can buy. The margherita was amazing, with fresh basil and mozzarella. I also loved the veggie so much. The pizza is seasoned well.

author: megan marckini
review_text: Walked in and staff immediately greeted my husband and I so kindly, food came out steaming hot and absolutely delicious. One of the best sandwiches I have ever had. A MUST.

author: Andrea Sarasin
review_text: This restaurant is a hidden treasure. The staff is always super friendly and treats you like family, the pizza is yummy and has so many good options and the prices are really fair. Our family loves coming here.

author: Marie Gail Stratford
review_text: Absolutely amazing local sandwich shop! We had the turkey and brie panini (seasonal) and a gluten-free Top-Shelf Italian. Both were amazing. I grabbed a carmel apple cookie for the road afterward as well. Fantastic place for families. Friendly neighborhood vibe.

author: Joshua Young
review_text: Fun local deli right next to a fire station, so you know the food is legit. Staffs were friendly. Portions were large. Grown-up Grilled Cheese was delicious. The BBQ brisket were tender and melts in my mouth. Steaktip sub was huge, my friend couldn't even finish. Can't go wrong with steak tips plus peppers and onions.

author: Yessi Bleu
review_text: I have been going here since I found it in 2013 and have been going wvwr since even when I have live 90min away of make ny way there its a plus my family lives in jamaica plain haha...I always get thr monster wrap Joe Spa with curly fries. This last time I went i got a wrap and a kids meal mozzarella sticks and fries and its a reasonable price

author: Gragor Joseph
review_text: I've always dined in at this location (Jamaica Plain), or ordered my food to-go while inside. Always great service, and so far, everything I've tried from them tastes amazing (mainly, the paninis and pizzas). I do plan to eventually make my way through most of their menu, eventually.

author: PT Payton
review_text: Will not return. Lots of menu items to choose from but we were sadly disappointed. Food is overpriced and sandwiches were soggy. French fries tasted like old fryer and cookies were stale. Service counter workers are rude and stare at you while you are eating not a very comfortable situation.

author: M Goldman
review_text: Best pizza in the neighborhood! Solid salads too. Everyone is nice and patient with the kids.

author: Raymond Green
review_text: This place is the " real deal " trust me, the food is amazing.. the workers Sophie, and Arielle. OMG they will take good care of you. They both are so nice get the orders right 👍 and take good care of the customers. They make u feel like your part of the " real deal " family thank you ladies... Please order from here.. the food is good I didn't get a chance to upload a photo...this business and staff are truly....... The Real Deal.....

author: Cecilia
review_text: Friendly staff, good prices and food. Turkey fig panini was amazing

author: Lemus Lemus
review_text: Very good place to bring family or friends. The food was good and had amazing service when I walked out without my sauce the lady came outside and gave it to me

author: Ellis Seul
review_text: Very good salads and sandwiches with generous portion sizes and fast and friendly service every time – they call this place the real deal for a reason!

author: KayyLynn
review_text: 2 HUGE specialty slices and a fountain drink for $10! Can't beat the price! Pizza was fresh and hot!

author: A P
review_text: I had grown up grilled cheese and it was so incredibly awful that it makes sense to review it, so that others can think twice before ordering this epic failure and wasting 14 dollars. It is basically two slices of toast, drowned in awful ketchup, with some meat (nothing to write home about), some cheese (likewise) and something that was supposed to be caramelised onion. It was sautéed onion, nowhere near caramelised onion. The sandwich looked bloody terrible, but I was hungry and I do not like wasting food, so I decided to eat it. It turned out to be a grave mistake, because it not only looked unappetising, but it also tasted truly terrible: just oily toast with loads of ketchup (literally drowned in it) with overpowering vinegary taste plus sautéed onions and some meat and some cheese. Given that it was drowned in this awful sauce, it could have been cardboard. After eating this, I felt like I ate a ton of bricks, plus it left a truly terrible taste in my mouth for a long time. Awful experience. I would never order this again. It is surprising, because it was recommended by staff as one of their most popular items on the menu

author: Alec Silva
review_text: got a seasonal specialty burger that was amazing and a salad that was really really good. Excellent portions can’t believe how awesome this food is!

author: Kristopher Kuss
review_text: The food is pretty good. The fried chicken sandwich was cooked well. Not much flavor going on other than the chicken. The spicy cheesy beef sandwich was tasty, only slightly spicy. The curly fries were well seasoned and crispy, but not hot. The regular fries were good.

author: Daniel Church
review_text: The staff at Real Deal are amazing. Always helpful, friendly, and efficient. The food is reliable and tasty - with plenty of gluten free options (including French fries made in a separate frier). We get takeout from here often and always enjoy it. Recommend!

author: Brooklyn Rose
review_text: THE SERVICE: Unremarkable customer service experience in alignment with an old school pub. Come as you are, take a seat, and we’ll get to you kind of establishment. The weathered decor is charming, and the atmosphere is nostalgic- I felt comfortable. THE FOOD: The fried seafood platter was very good. The seafood tasted fresh, and the batter perfectly adhered giving the ideal non-greasy coating. I particularly liked the fact that the seasoning accentuated the natural flavors of the seafood. The clam bellies and scallops were my standout bites. The side green beans tasted invisible because the only adornment was steam. The onion rings were cooked to perfection-light and crunchy batter encasing a succulent onion. THE VALUE: Budget friendly price point for fresh well prepared seafood.

author: Roscoe Gay
review_text: Galway House: A Hidden Gem That Delivers Big Tucked away in the neighborhood for decades, Galway House is the kind of spot locals swear by. The food? Always flavorful. The drinks? On point. And the portions? Generous enough to satisfy any appetite. Best part prices that respect your wallet without skimping on quality. If you haven’t been, you’re missing out on one of the area’s best-kept secrets.

author: Frank Fazzalari
review_text: The Galway House in Boston sure takes you back — this place started in 1960, and that’s exactly what it feels like walking in. We were greeted by a few servers almost immediately — it felt good to know you were recognized. We grabbed ourselves a booth, ordered a few pints and some wine, and then put in our food order. We had the seafood platter — broiled (key, not fried). Wow — it had about 8 scallops, shrimp, and a nice piece of fish — all tasty. We also ordered the steak tips — they were great. I think they use the same marinade I make. Steamed broccoli, summer squash, mashed potatoes, mac and cheese, and fries rounded out the sides. Oh, get this — for an extra $2, you can add the clam chowder when you order a main, so we definitely opted for that. All in all, it was a good experience, and I would definitely go back. Saluti

author: Elena Winell
review_text: One of those rare places where every single thing on the menu is top notch. I took a friend here who noticed their "Liver, Bacon, and Onions" entree on the menu and ordered it purely on the logic of "It's a ballsy dish to list...they clearly wouldn't list it if it weren't amazing." His hunch was right. My go-to is the chicken parm sub, but whenever I've ordered anything else I haven't been disappointed. Wide selection of good beers. Service quality depends on the time of day and the server you get, but I haven't been kept waiting for longer than 10 minutes at the most here. The more seasoned servers are actually kind of amazing to watch because of how efficient they are. Easily the best pub in JP, especially with the prices! Also the posters are really fun. They have one that looks like a diagram from an ENT's office but the words are the lyrics to 'Comfortably Numb'

author: Brooks Reeves
review_text: This cozy Irish/American/Italian(??) pub exceeded my expectations. I admit, this kind of generic American pub fare is not at all my favorite, but I went with a friend. I ordered the soup of the day (escarole) and a cheeseburger. The escarole was definitely the highlight (not bad for three bucks!) and my cheeseburger was definitely above average. The steak fries were under seasoned, but nothing a personal application of salt and pepper couldn’t fix. To be clear, this bar is not promising anything it can’t deliver. I’m confused why it’s an Irish pub when the entire menu seems clearly Italian/American. Pasta, steak, and seafood (broiled or fried). It was definitely well attended the Friday lunch I came in, and the staff was friendly and cheerful, if a bit swamped. If you are in the mood for above average American bar-food fare it’s definitely a strong option. I doubt its menu has changed in decades, but I think for a certain clientele that’s probably appreciated.

author: Barbara Smith
review_text: My friend whom I always meet up with when I visit Boston always chose this place. Learning he passed within the last week, I honored his memory by grabbing a bowl of chowder, our normal prelude to their lobster. It was creamier than I had remembered, served with oyster crackers than put it over the top. Truly one of the best in New Dngland if you are in the camp that prizes rich vs.soupy. Paired with a quick Guiness it was heaven. It did take a bit to get service with two regulars getting priority. Waiting on a rideshare I was a bit annoyed, but stuck it out for a taste of my ling-time former home. Hit the spot.

author: Christa Dunn
review_text: We enjoyed our food- enormous serving sizes and very reasonable prices!

author: Being Fancy Entertainment
review_text: This was me and my cousins first time. The food was good and the servings were big while the prices was cheap. The service was amazing and I will definitely be returning. The stuff mushrooms was so good.

author: Zarii Parra
review_text: Amazing local place. Guinness on tap ! Service on point and the clam chower is really good. Real people work here so don't be surprise if they act like humans an not just like service robots

author: World Traveler
review_text: This place 3 years ago was wonderful Great service, amazing food and good times This time 11/624 the bartender kept complaining about the customers asking questions etc, the food is just ok now. It's not the fun atmosphere it used to have. I will probably not return. Sad for me ***I should add that if you are a local, it's a different experience. They will take care of you better if you are a regular customer.

author: Lourin Costa
review_text: This place is my best places for food everything is prepared fresh and the baked potatoes with rack of baby ribs or steak is so good I love the clam chowder and the prices so reasonable not expensive quality size is pretty good I will give a 5 star for food and prices

author: Mia Marroquin
review_text: Stumbled upon this gem and couldn’t not be happier with our decision. The wings, burger, onion rings and clam chowder were out of this world. Bartender was so friendly and attentive. Couldn’t recommend this place enough.

author: Konstantinos Tziallas
review_text: On our Travels through Jamaica Plain we stopped at The Galway House for dinner. It's a Cozy Neighborhood Pub. We sat down at the bar and ordered some 😋Buffalo Chicken Wings 😋 and Ice Cold Drinks 🍹🍻 ❄️ the wings were Delicious 😋. We ordered the Blue Cheese Burger Special 😋 which was Tasty. The Service was Great 👍 Definitely Recommend Galway House!

author: 6CRAN
review_text: Place is packed. Very narrow on the bar side and nice size booths on the dine in side. Great prices. Lots of bang for your buck. I get the fish and chip which is always fresh. Great drinks. This is that neighborhood feel. Diverse crowd. Prices cannot be beat

author: Chelsea Adams
review_text: Always feel welcome and food is always reliable comfort go-to. Waitress was friendly made our 10 month old happy with smiles and encouragement! Will go again the next time we need a night out of the house.

author: O. G.
review_text: Denise was awesome, we had a family dinner. We all enjoyed everything. Perfect place for food and drinks.

author: sahand sb
review_text: What you get for the price is great! Clam Chowder was tasty! Cozy neighborhood type bar and food!

author: Sunny Day
review_text: Visiting from another state. Came here with some friends who told me this was the best place for fried clams which I was craving for. They said order the seafood platter which comes with the best clam chowder. The place was packed. We were squished waiting at the front door which was the only place to wait until your name was called. My opinion, it was like a hole in the wall where locals gather. (Nothing wrong with that. ) The waitress was pleasant but extremely busy. We all ordered the fried seafood platter plate. It wasn't long before our food arrived. As soon as the plate was sat before I was immediately disappointed. I really wanted fried clams and they gave me 4 clams with the bellies, 4 shrimp, 3 scallops and 2 half pieces of fish. I was looking for a plate overflowing with these items since it's called a platter. Tasting every item including the clam chowder left me disappointed as there was no good seasonings that I liked on any of the food. The only thing I enjoyed was the fries. I'm leaving this spot to the locals who seemed to really enjoy the food while my search continues for great fried clams in Boston.

author: Jennifer Denise (Lulu bell)
review_text: It was nice love the service the food was so much on the plate had to bring hm leftover...Good affordable prices an get there early when we left line at the door, two thumbs up u want good food an nice service an outgoing layback atmosphere, date night after the club food or just to hang out for a drink..😊👍👍

author: Walter Swoboda
review_text: Great service... one of the best chill bowls. The strawberry dessert was wonderful. I spent 5 days in Boston... 3 nights of them spent eating there. All around great

author: Christa West
review_text: I’ve had mixed experiences at Jadu.. my regular order is a small regular milk iced latte, often with a syrup flavor ($7+) which I find to be a steep price for the quality of the drink and area/competitor cafes. The atmosphere is bright and welcoming, but the staff at the register are often stand-offish. The most recent latte I tried at Jadu was unfortunately a huge miss and the flavors were way off. I usually have no problem speaking up for myself but the impersonal impression I’ve received from the staff made me decide to bit my tongue. Unsure if I will be trying again.

author: Tyler Cumella
review_text: My husband and I have been to Jadu a few times for coffee, breakfast, and pastries, and have been delighted each time. We recently went for their dinner/wine service, though, and loved it even more! Our server was lovely and provided great recommendations. The food was delicious and the portions allowed us to try a bunch of menu items. The vibe was cozy. We're so glad to have a spot like this in JP.

author: Kelsey Munger
review_text: Jadu has been such an amazing addition to our neighborhood! The owner Maya is the sweetest and the staff and vibes are equally as wonderful :) delicious food and fun drink menu - you gotta check out their wine bar at night too!

author: J W
review_text: Very cute minimalist trendy decor. Very bright! There’s designated laptop and non-laptop seating too. I only came for lunch but the Maggi Deluxe was delicious!!!

author: Raj
review_text: Extremely cute cafe - I can't wait to try their wine selection, I've heard extremely positive things about where they source their wine. It's a small cute coffee shop most days of the week and then Th-Sat in the nights they are a wine bar. It's a really nice space. The iced Americano was well made and the food smelled quite good inside. I would highly recommend this spot in JP.

author: Amanda Ferreira
review_text: Absolutely loved my visit to Jadu Cafe! The food was fantastic – the Avo Tartine was a standout, fresh and flavorful with just the right balance of textures. The brownies were also perfect – rich, gooey, and indulgent. The staff were incredibly friendly and welcoming, which made the experience even better. A perfect spot for a cozy brunch or coffee break!

author: Jea Kim
review_text: South Asian/Middle Eastern-inspired cafe that brings a refreshing concept to JP, but its execution feels like a work in progress. Came here for breakfast and lunch this past week. On my first visit for breakfast, I opted for the pistachio butter toast and Breakfast Sammy. The toast had a promising start — the nutty richness of pistachio butter paired beautifully with fragrant rose petals. Yet, the tartness tipped the balance and made it difficult to finish without the grounding comfort of their turmeric latte. As for the Breakfast Sammy, it was a solid option. The focaccia was fine, though not my personal favorite for a sandwich base, and I found myself wishing for a more generous slather of Calabrian chili butter to elevate the flavors. I then returned with a friend for lunch and tried the Turkish-style eggs and Chicken & Rice. The Turkish eggs was essentially a deconstructed breakfast pita — jammy eggs, garlic labneh, and Aleppo pepper oil delivered on comfort but lacked a distinctive twist. Meanwhile, the Chicken & Rice offered a satisfying salad-rice bowl hybrid. The peanut ginger marinade added a nice twist, yet the dish was oddly similar to something I tasted from DIG. Overall, the cafe undoubtedly has potential, with thoughtful touches and a welcoming vibe. Not sure if I would return just for the food, but definitely a great spot to casually hang out with friends.

author: Cameron
review_text: Such a cute gem in JP! Jada is a beautiful cafe that feels so light and bright and welcoming. All their food looks so beautiful and is actually unique and flavorful! The savory oats were an excellent start to the day, the jammy eggs melding perfectly with the chili crisp and miso flavors. The staff were also so nice, and I love that they have a few tables kept as laptop-free, making it a nice mix of people working or just chatting/reading. My only slight fault is the Maple Ginger Latte. A good drink, just really no maple or ginger flavor, just a good latte. Still, I would absolutely recommend coming here to hang out for a few hours, and don’t pass on the food!

author: John D
review_text: Great quick breakfast and lunch selections with some really nice specialty coffee and tea options. It can get pretty crowded here and the line to order can get a little awkward when it’s busy. The new wine bar is a lot of fun. You can treat it as a before/after dinner stop or make a whole evening out of it. Reservations on Resy might be required for awhile, as it seems pretty popular. Overall a great place to grab food and drink.

author: Caroline Auger
review_text: Amazing new cafe! Such a beautiful space, and the staff is helpful & kind. The food is delicious! We got the Turkish style eggs, chicken & rice, and the mezze situation. Everything I've had so far is perfect!

author: Michael Chmielewski
review_text: This is a great new coffee shop in JP. Small intimate space which gets pretty busy even during the week. The coffee is very good and I’ve really enjoyed the Turkish style eggs, and breakfast sandwich. Update: went to one of their first nights as a wine bar and it was awesome! Very impressed with their selection of wines. Snacks we had included meatballs and feta dip. We tried a red, orange, white and rose which were all fresh. Will definitely be added to our regular wine spots. Recommend resys as its a very small spot but there is limited walkin counter space.

author: Rebecca
review_text: Jamaica plain has needed a bigger coffee shop that isn’t a chain! I’m thrilled that we now have somewhere to work and lounge. It’s a great addition to the neighborhood. It’s also a unique concept, with Indian inspired snacks and beverages. The Cardamom Clove latte is perfect and a large quantity. It’s truly some of the best coffee I’ve had in Boston in a long time and is perfectly balanced. I also tried their breakfast sandwich with Calabrian chili oil butter, which was tasty, but a bit small. I can’t wait to try their other offerings.

author: GT
review_text: High quality drinks and food, but service is incredibly slow. I waited 20 minutes for a latte. I appreciate a chill atmosphere, but the staff loves to chat more than get orders out efficiently - I think there can be a better balance. Not the spot to run in and get a quick drink at the moment, which is unfortunate because they’re the only spot with hojicha!

author: Salokya Sarira
review_text: I got the Orange Blossom Honey Latte, Maple Ginger Latte, and the Labneh Parfait. I really enjoyed their lattes as they are really smooth and balanced. However, the orange blossom one was better as the orange blossom elevated the flavors. I could barely taste the ginger in the other one. The Labneh Parfait is stunning! The creamy and whipped yoghurt is luscious and is elevated by the tartness of the pomegranate molasses and the crunch of the hemp crumble! I wish they still had the Cardamom Clove Latte (seasonal latte) as I had heard good things about it and wanted to try it.

author: Amanda Fazekas
review_text: Really cute place to grab a coffee and some food! The coffee was high quality and made very well, and the iced latte was HUGE. Also tried their breakfast sandwich which was good too. It has a very modern vibe and friendly staff and is a nice spot to sip on your coffee for a while.

author: Joseph Capatosto
review_text: Another great reason to head to JP, I love this simple menu with so many options for savory and sweet for breakfast and lunch. They have great coffee and a bright open space. Try all the little things that you don’t know what they are. I can’t wait until they have a wine program and I can stay all day long.

author: M M
review_text: Small pours at the wine bar :( … I enjoyed the variety within the 20ish wine selection. Props for having a wine from New England. I hope they get a much deeper selection as a wine bar. Servers were kind, but I’m not sure if they have any knowledge of wine. Food was good. Wish the wine prices were $9-14, rather than $14-22 for a glass… especially with the small pours. I guess the reasonable food prices make up for it.

author: Aiden Nguyen
review_text: The new kid on the block!!! Came here on a Monday afternoon, and it was bustling with people working on their laptops and chatting with friends. Sad I wasn't able to grab a seat, but it's another opportunity to come back 😉 I love that the owner came out and greeted me and my friends 🥰 I appreciate the thoughtful selection of products in the store. I can't wait to come back! Support your local business ✨️💕🫶🏼

author: Daniel Davies
review_text: A beautiful space with an inventive menu. However, drinks and food service were incredibly slow. It took 25 mins for drinks to be ready and a further 10 mins for the food. The staff told us we’d need to leave very shortly after receiving our food as they were closing. We would have appreciate a grace period seeing as it took so long for our food to arrive.

author: Suzi
review_text: Stopped by Jadu on opening day to get the lay of the land, and they so did not disappoint! The latte ($5) was creamy and came out at a drinkable temp, and the avocado tartine ($11, $13 with jammy egg add on) was divine: crunchy crust, flavorful avocado spread, perfectly soft egg. They did just a light sprinkle of the spice topping for me and it was perfect. While I normally stick to coffee, Jadu breakfast will be going in the rotation for when I want to treat myself!

author: Meri Slaughter
review_text: Are lunch here with a friend and it was a perfect place to catch up. I have a dairy allergy, so they made me a Monument sandwich with no cheese - it was a little overpowered by the tart cranberries and green apple. I'll try a different sandwich next time. The side of potatoes are delicious! I did get a vegan carrot cake cupcake and it was phenomenal 😍 staff is knowledgeable about their menu and had no problem navigating my allergy. Will be back!

author: Samantha Diaz
review_text: First off the German chocolate cake.. SO DELISH!! It’s so rich and moist and they’re very generous with the coconut topping, 20/10 dessert choice!! The footlight I got was delish!! They were so nice and subbed my turkey instead of bacon!! It was so worth it!! My friend got the Italian mache was super delish as well!!

author: Andrew costa
review_text: If you’re looking for the best coffee shop in Jamaica Plain, Massachusetts, this bakery is the place to be. The breakfast here is absolutely fantastic—fresh, flavorful, and the perfect way to start your day. Their pastries are hands down the best in Jamaica Plain, with every bite tasting homemade and baked to perfection. What really sets this spot apart is the people. The owner, Charlie, is truly a diamond in the rough—down-to-earth, welcoming, and passionate about what he does. The staff reflects the same warmth and friendliness, making every visit feel special. One of my favorite parts about this Jamaica Plain bakery and café is the cozy spot in the back where you can sit down with your coffee, relax, and enjoy the atmosphere. It’s a wonderful hidden gem in the neighborhood, perfect for breakfast, coffee dates, or just a quiet moment with a pastry and a latte. I highly recommend this bakery to anyone in or around Jamaica Plain. Whether you’re local or just visiting, make sure to stop in—you’ll be glad you did!

author: Matt H
review_text: We’ve been here a bunch of times as they have great vegan sandwich options. The ‘steak bomb’ sandwich is one of the best vegan sandwiches you can get around Boston. The rest are hit or miss. Some of the baked good are underwhelming which is why I’m only giving a 4

author: Lexia Cicone
review_text: We got a vegan wedding cake from Fiore's Bakery. Pros: The cake was very affordable, looked beautiful, and tasted amazing. Even our non-vegan guests commented on how good it was! We also loved that they offered gluten-free cupcakes for our guests with dietary restrictions. Cons: The ordering process was unfortunately quite disorganized. We received a call on the day of pickup asking what design we wanted, even though we had confirmed the details with an employee several months earlier. When we re-sent the design that had already been approved, the employee responded in a rude manner, and we felt the response was unnecessarily defensive. More particularly, the employee dismissed our concerns on the phone, continued to cut us off, and attempted to gaslight us into thinking that we caused the miscommunication (despite showing screenshots of our continual communication with our point of contact at the bakery about our design for over a year). While the end result was wonderful, the experience leading up to it was stressful. I’d recommend Fiore’s for their delicious vegan cakes, but would be cautious about using them for weddings, and suggest confirming design details multiple times to avoid any last-minute confusion.

author: Rick Lu
review_text: Open early on Sunday morning...enjoyed blueberry scones and the raspberry filled crispy turnover.

author: Garrett R
review_text: This is one of my favorite lunch spots, especially as someone with a gluten allergy. They have lots of gluten-free options. I got the Christopher Robin on a gluten-free bagel and it was delicious. Sandwiches come with a small side of salad and breakfast potatoes which are both really good. I normally order ahead as it can be very busy in there. Seating can be limited because it is extremely popular and the inside is not huge so best to plan ahead. Would very much recommend.

author: Florencia Rojas-Miguez
review_text: The food used to be good. Now it’s inedible. I don’t know if they changed the baker and chef but this place isn’t as good as it used to be. We didn’t finish our food. Really disappointed that this place lost its quality.

author: Achyut Shrestha
review_text: Once I discovered this place, I stopped cooking at home! Best vegan sandwiches, great price, good people!

author: Steve Sharp
review_text: Had a great breakfast sandwich with potatoes, salad and tasty coffee. Staff were very friendly and helpful Great deal for tasty food.

author: Buggie
review_text: Delicious food, not too expensive, good many for your buck. They also sell very pretty potted plants and the chairs are painted like flowers

author: Katherine Kisner (Kat)
review_text: Great food. I didn’t expect it to come with sides, but it was a pleasant surprise.

author: lara tang
review_text: They have the BIGGEST ice coffees lol! And I like the sandwiches on fresh bread. I like the avocado and the omelettes. Nice spot for breakfast!!!! I think the potatoes they come with are little weak like they’re never crispy but it’s free potato and not a bag of chips so that’s better. And I brought a cake to a house party and everyone loved it. So get the sandwiches they’re not a bad price.

author: A Dan
review_text: Love Fiore's. Each sandwhich comes with a nice lil side salad and some solid potatoes. My BF is a vegetarian and obsessed with the Vegan BLT. Meanwhile, I love their Christopher Robin, its a nice refreshing sandwhich. The folks are super friendly and its always such a child environment. Normally can get my order nice and quick. A true JP gem.

author: Alma Laraxadu
review_text: I’ve been getting delicious vegan cakes here for my son’s birthday the last few years. I always get the vanilla one and it NEVER disappoints. Probably one of the best cakes I ever tasted. definitely the best vegan cake I have ever come across. They also always have it ready on time. Thanks Fiore for making my kids birthday that much more special every year. Anytime I need cake this is where I will be heading. It’s so good I may not even wait for a special occasion haha :)

author: Vzar zack
review_text: Walked in and ignored for 10 minutes by someone walking back-and-forth with new items for the display case. Not even a hello, I’ll be with you in a minute. Forced to walk out when they disappeared to the back.

author: Kathy B.
review_text: Best breakfast sandwich in JP. Generous and delicious scrambled eggs, cheese, and sausage or bacon with tomato on your choice of bagel. Accompanying home fries are perfect along with lightly dressed greens.

author: Ben Aronson
review_text: EDIT: I appreciate what they are doing with their “rice & beans” pop-up, increasing a star Cute, homey neighborhood coffee shop with some thoughtful additions. The cakes look impressive, though I haven’t tried, and I think it’s super cool that they have various dinner pop-ups serving different parts of the community. I always appreciate a locally-owned coffee shop that opens their space for people to gather and this is the only one in the neighborhood. That being said, the coffee is only ok and the two or three pasties I’ve tried, including the scones, were seriously underwhelming. In the several times I’ve visited I have also not felt welcomed by the staff. I don’t need baristas to be singing hello but when I have other options, having a warm smile and an inviting feel makes a difference. Maybe the staff aren’t too happy there, idk, but my experience has turned me off from coming here.

author: Jann Elaine Eleodinmuo
review_text: I've tried this place a few times but sadly the coffee usually tastes burnt. The prices are reasonable. The atmosphere is cute; I love the plants. The guy who works there most of the time always seems like he doesn't need to be friendly and he's way too cool to serve anyone anyway, that it's annoying and inconvenient for him to have to do so. The bakery options- so many of them are vegan or gluten-free but if you're looking for normal stuff there aren't as many options, which is weird because traditionally a "bakery" sells things that INCLUDE flour and butter. But mostly the coffee having a bad aftertaste bothers me.

author: Mercedes Reid
review_text: So... I ordered a cake for a birthday dinner. I was rushed off of the phone by the person taking my order. I guess the store was busy??? Anyway, I asked for fresh fruit on my cake to which she told me it would be an extra charge, I said that it'd be fine and asked for strawberries. The cake had NO STRAWBERRIES AT ALL. So why did she charge me extra? Also, the cake was kind of dry. I felt so bad because it was a special birthday and the cake was the worst part of the experience. I normally order from here every year and this is my first complaint. I'm so disappointed. 😔

author: Justin Snider
review_text: Great local bar. Came on a Saturday to watch football and it wasnt super busy. Only had a few things on the menu but they were all good. Would definitely come back.

author: Marie Gail Stratford
review_text: Perfect place to unwind at the end of a long day! I've recently moved into the neighborhood and was taking a walk after a long afternoon of virtual meetings. Stopped for a glass of wine and a nibble. The bartenders were both attentive and wonderful, making sure I had what I needed and felt welcome in the space. The food was good--especially the sweet potato fries. I will definitely be back!

author: Doron Bracha
review_text: It's a nice down to earth neighborhood pub, conveniently located on a main street. Pretty good bar, decent food for a pub, at very reasonable prices. Comfortable seating, clean restrooms. We enjoyed a comedy show on a winter Saturday night. Yet I can't rate it 5 stars due to a few things. The interior decor is not as rich as in other pubs. They held our credit card thru the evening, which we never saw in other places. It made me uncomfortable thinking that they could take pictures of my card and use it as they wish. I understand they're afraid that people would run off without paying, but in this case they had all my info since I bought the comedy tickets online. After the comedy show, we couldn't stay much longer for more food, drinks and conversation, because they played very loud music, so we left. Good experience overall :-)

author: Jason Mackinnon
review_text: Had an incredible meal here! The burger was juicy, flavorful, and cooked just the way i ordered. Easily one of the best I’ve had in a long time. I also came in late when they were on "fried food only" but the owner made me a burger regardless. What really made the experience even better was the service. Crystal was amazing—super friendly, attentive, and had multiple check ins with me. Top notch service.

author: Stefanie Nicolosi
review_text: Their Chicken fingers and fries do not disappoint. Karaoke is a fun time. The drinks were lackluster but we didn't even arrive until after midnight. Staff was likely just trying to control overdrinking. Reasonable prices and fun history. All around good time.

author: Tom Duffy
review_text: One of the best local pubs I’ve been to flying out of Logan stopped to visit. My niece came to Jeannie’s ordered some food but the grill was not on the owner. Hank said if you’ll be here a while, I’ll fire it up and cook for you. it doesn’t get any better, the food is fantastic as well as the selection of adult beverages Can’t wait to stop back gotta try the chili. Thanks Hank

author: Mich Bartolo
review_text: Sep 2024: For bar food, it was great. The fried ravioli was delicious and perfectly crispy. The fries were evenly cut and fresh, and the burgers were decent for a bar. The local drinks were a nice touch as well.

author: Kayla Nygaard
review_text: This place has a great vibe. The staff are so friendly and made sure to get me my food even when I changed seats. And the food (I got the warm pretzel app) was so good. Definitely going to be back to try more!

author: D.
review_text: First time here and it was very nice. Everyone knew each other and the bartender. I found out that the menu that's on the website is about 3 or more years out of date. So they have a new menu at the bar to look at. Not a bad place to stop in to from time to time.

author: J H
review_text: I was an out of towner who needed a place to sit for a couple hours while I waited on a medical emergency to be resolved, and I didn't feel unwelcome here. This place had delicious fried pickles, cold beer, and by chance I stumbled in on Stand Up Comedy Night, so I had a few good laughs. Turned a crummy night into a good one, so thanks.

author: CKBates AKA Farm Grammy
review_text: Fun and surprising. Great stand up comedy in a small venue. Reasonable tasty food and Guinness well poured.

author: V P
review_text: I love coming here karaoke nights on Saturday, the Dj is good, drinks are good. Got Jell-O shots and drinks, yummy bar food. Cheaper than most places and a good time

author: Nuno Barbosa
review_text: Food was great. Bar tender was terrible! We were there for the open mic comedy night which is through RANDOM PICKS OUT OF RAFT BOX. As soon as the host noticed that we were a large group he asked for the name and just kept the card for the WHOLE NIGHT! Just so they could keep us around until the end of the night! That was a terrible experience! We could’ve definitely hung around after our friends set but the fact that they played us to stay just shows the type of people who run this business.

author: Artem Aleksanyan
review_text: I came for trivia, drinks and bar food. This bar would be perfectly fine except for the fact that they WILL NOT SERVE TAP WATER, instead offering plastic bottles of water for $1.50! Who does that?? I am shocked it is not against the law to serve food and alcohol without tap water for free but here we are. Apparently every other sit down restaurant, bar, and coffee shop I’ve ever been to in MA has been just doing it on good will. Shame these guys did not get the memo to be normal good guys. So disappointing.

author: travis stirewalt
review_text: April 20th, 2024: It should be noted that this establishment does NOT serve WATER. I kid you not… They’ll only sell you bottled water at a premium. This is the first time in 30 years I’ve patronized a bar that won’t give you a glass of water after ordering 50 dollars worth of food & alcohol. I spoke to the owner (Hank) regarding the policy and he was incredibly rude & almost proud of it. He said it was “the way of the future”. Well in the very near future (Monday morning) I’ll be reporting this to the city of Boston as I believe it’s unlawful to deny paying customers (or human beings in general) a simple glass of tap water. Pure greed, in such an inhumane fashion…

author: Jose Rodriguez
review_text: Awesome Pub and grill, the bartender was very attentive and the locals were very welcoming. A comedian by the name of Pierre made great conversation right off the back and welcome us in.

author: Molly Pratt
review_text: My friends of color call this "the racist place". On multiple occasions we have experienced microagressions directed towards us by multiple employees. If you are not white, be prepared to be treated rudely. Even though the food was good, we will but be going back.

author: Sumaiya Miah
review_text: racist and homophobic. joe told my friends from mexico "welcome to america" before they kicked us out. wish i could give negative stars. i will not be visiting again

author: Brian McCaffrey
review_text: Good pub food, a friendly and relaxed vibe, nice staff. Cozy neighborhood spot with live music, karaoke, and comedy nights.

author: Debra Doyle
review_text: The bartender was very rude! She had horrible customer service skills! I will not be going back there!

author: Rithvik
review_text: I recently had a meal at Brassica, and overall, it was a great experience. The risotto was creamy and flavorful, and the pizza had a wonderfully thin crust, very much like a classic New York-style pizza. The rigatoni pasta was tasty, though not particularly standout, but still a solid choice. The fried rice was packed with flavor and really hit the spot. The BK fried chicken (we ordered the larger portion) was incredibly tender and had just the right amount of sweetness served with a small portion of homemade mustard sauce on the side and lemon wedges, it was definitely a winner. However, the real star of the show was the Brussels sprouts. They were absolutely fantastic, crispy, perfectly seasoned, and bursting with flavor. Definitely the dish that left the biggest impression, and I’ll be coming back just for those!

author: Steve Gonyaw
review_text: Loved the experience. The atmosphere, the food, the service…. All tops! Even on a packed Saturday night, my date and I never felt the pressure or stress of a busy night. Staff was warm and welcoming. Bartenders were fun and very fast with orders, they seem to love their jobs and that goes a long way for guests.

author: Ashley Farias
review_text: The service was excellent. Staff was friendly, attentive and informative. I ordered the fried rice from their brunch menu and my sister ordered the melted butter pancakes. She loved the pancakes. While I enjoyed their unique touch to the fried rice and perfectly runny egg, I didn't love how much oil it was all swimming in. We also waited 45 min for our food. Edit: I made I a typo and wrote "informal" but really I meant "informative"🤦‍♀️ Learning that they just expanded and were adjusting to the new space is great context for helping me understand the delay!

author: Hannagh Jacobsen
review_text: Amazing food! Have been here before but first time in the new space. The brunch is so good, get the fresh hot sauce or else you’ll regret it. The house hot sauce is especially important for the chicken and waffles. The service is great as it’s always been. The new space is much more comfortable but I wish the lighting were a little softer for those of us sitting at tables. 10/10 my favorite brunch restaurant in Boston.

author: Emma Reading
review_text: This was such a fun dining experience! It's a very eclectic array of foods with so many flavors to try. Our server, Josh, said the best way to describe the food they serve was "saucy" and that honestly is true. So many good sauces, with flavors from all over the world! We did The Ride, a fixed menu with 8 plates plus dessert. They were flexible with some dietary needs and our server was fun, knowledgeable, and had fantastic service. We loved trying so many different things and enjoyed some lovely cocktails alongside it all. Such a great spot to try new flavors and have a special date night!

author: Eagle Bound
review_text: We went for brunch and overall had a good time. We got the pretzel biscuit, brown butter pancakes, omelette, and breakfast fried rice. Everything looked great and the food did taste good, but towards the end of our meal we did start to feel it was a bit greasy and heavy. The vegetarian options were extensive, which I really appreciated. I would come back if I wanted to take some friends, but I think it’s slightly out of my budget to become a regular option.

author: Doron Bracha
review_text: I'm sorry to write that our experience was mediocre and disappointing. We went there with another couple of friends for dinner on a Friday evening in mid August. The place was full of people, apparently having a good time. The staff was busy and diligent, kind and friendly. The location is not so nice and the exteriors are somewhat rough, between a central bus station on a busy street with traffic and honking cars, and a parking lot of a funeral home, with big trash dumpsters. We sat in the back yard tent, four people around a small table with small plates. We liked the concept of sharing various plates and dishes, but the portions were small and the food was very salty and greasy (gave me heartburn). The black cod was unpleasantly smelly (fishy), and the green salad was very bitter and salty. The only way to fill my tummy was to order some bread, which was served with way too much butter, really wasteful. I saw a picture of fries in a review online and asked the waitress why it wasn't on the menu, she smiled and said it's a secret... she also suggested the special of the day, but did not tell us the price, and that was not on the menu either. As a matter of principle and practicality, all items should be on the menu, and customers should know the prices before placing orders. The prices are pretty high and they charge around 23% fee to cover gratuity for the waiters, kitchen and bar staff. We respect and support all those good people, but do not like to be charged such high fees. Either raise the prices and show them clearly on the menu, or take whatever tips people leave and split the money between all the employees. Customers should have the freedom to decide how much they want to tip, considering the quality of food and service they received. We enjoyed spending a couple hours with our friends, but did not enjoy the food or sitting on the asphalt in the undecorated tent, with loud background noise. For us, it was not worth $40 per person (with no meat or seafood, with no dessert or coffee); there are much nicer places at that price level.

author: Candice Springer
review_text: Brassica has one of the best brunches in town. The cocktails are wonderful and the food is top-notch. I love their commitment to changing up the flavors just enough to keep you wanting more, but also keeping their tried and true gems on the menu (shout out to the chicken and waffles)! And, I always look forward to taking home one of their homeade doughnuts for later. They never miss!

author: Lillie Marshall
review_text: Awesome experience trying The Ride (their epic tasting menu) at their new larger location! Delicious, fun food, lovely staff, and great vibe. Incredible deal for how much food you get — I took home most of a pizza (never seen a whole pizza in a multi-course tasting menu!) and entire second dessert. Eating the leftovers the next day was wonderful, too! Highly recommend.

author: Sahra
review_text: Brassica is a truly unique restaurant and cafe. We went for brunch and were met with a warm quirky Brooklyn ambiance with high hopes for the food. We started with two donuts to share- a toasted maple donut and a Boston cream (can’t remember the specific names) but they were absolutely delicious and fresh. We also ordered the fried rice with fried chicken, which was packed with flavor Umami and spice-absolutely incredible. We also ordered the tamales which tasted truly authentic and the impossible burger. However, nothing compared to the hashbrowns, never have I tasted anything so deluxe and cheesy! We were all so satisfied and will come back again.🙏

author: Matt Sanda
review_text: Get the Detroit pizza. You can tell they have perfected the dough. It gives Tonino a run for their money! New location is spacious. Food is delicious. Cocktails are great. Cheaper than it seems on paper because gratuity is included in the prices.

author: Meaghan Kavanagh
review_text: We had a good time at Brassica. The staff were great and organized. The food was good but some things like the brussel sprouts were mid for the price and very small portions with rice underneath (seemed like they were just trying to cut costs). Also the pizza was alittle burnt, beyond what I would have served. But I loved the housemade vermouths and would recommend if you are looking for a fancy meal out in Boston that has a friendly/local vibe. Also definitely make a reso as it's a busy place.

author: Anastasia Ekman
review_text: A small piece of pork belly that fits in a hand palm, topped with a marshmallow, no side whatsoever - $28. An extremely thin and very simple tomato-mozzarella pizza, small - $30. Cocktails - all around $20 It feels like a joke. Interior and stuff are nice. But these prices are unacceptable. If at least we would see some craft in the presentation or something very special about the ingredients. They kept pushing us to order more plates. No thank you. Editing after the restaurant’s response: I know what I ordered! The tomato-mozzarella pizza aka Detroit for $29.50. Saying that I’m unable to see the craft is an interesting assumption. I have lived and eaten in many culinary capitals of this world and I know what high-level craft looks like. Also, by saying this you are putting down some great local eats that serve fresh and yummy food for much less $.

author: James Douthit
review_text: Our group of 4 vegetarians went here and were utterly blown away by the taste. We got biscuits-and-tofu, veg sausage big mac, brunch fried rice, and tamale. Every piece of tofu had an impressively delicate but flavorful breading and the tofu inside was also brined and tasty by itself. This is some of the best food I’ve ever had in Boston out of over 50 restaurants I’ve been to, and it was all vegetarian. The gravy on the biscuits was a special highlight, it might be gross but we literally licked the plate clean.

author: Ellen B Cutler
review_text: Saw Brassica recommended in the Boston Globe--among other restaurants--for a visit from the Michelin people. A foodie cousin was all in for a visit. We both took the T, she a couple of stops in JP, me, a bit more of a trek from East Boston. So getting there without a car is easy-peasy. We had reservations although probably not required on a Wednesday at 5:30. Charming. Casual. A bit noisy. Our server was prompt with drinks and explained the recommended approach: plates are small, so share. Foodie cousin and I opted for 3 plates: sole, flatbread margarita, salad. Weren't sure how much food it would be and it was plenty. Server started us on the fish and brought pizza and salad together. Perfect! Not cheap but excellent value. A wonderful time was had all round. We'll be back.

author: Marek Michalak
review_text: One of the best hidden gems on the Greater Boston culinary map! Food: Small tasting plates are the love language in this place and boy, they are wonderful! Most of them being Asian-fusion influenced. From the wonderful gochujang mackerel through one of the best brussell sprouts I've ever eaten to my absolute fave - the chive cakes with two types of curry sauce. WOW WOW WOW! One of the best dished I've had all year. Their cocktails are also fun and inventive. Service & Ambiance: Our waiter was absolutely wonderful - warm, friendly and made us feel right at home. I loved the interactions (though I usually find them awkward and forced) and it did feel like I was being welcomed into a spot owned by inclusive and quirky friends. It feels like a bar, a cafe and an upscale restaurant mixed together and I loved this low key vibe from the get-go. If you don't go there, you are really missing out!

author: Laura DeYoung
review_text: Phenomenal meal tonight - thank you!!! We went for “The Ride” - and enjoyed every dish. Tons of flavors, and this was an incredible value to get to try “a bit of everything”, plus the creamiest Tiramisu ever. The standouts for me were: Endive Salad, the Fish Collars, And the Pork Belly. Yum yum yum!! Thank you for s lovely evening, in a fun space. Our servers were all incredibly friendly and good pacing.

author: Matthew Gall
review_text: Went for The Ride for 2...very enjoyable experience for a first visit. 9 courses (which included dessert) of shared plates. Really enjoyed some unique flavor pairings. Our server and rest of staff were great too.

author: N M
review_text: My family and I had dinner at Brassica last Sat. Would highly highly recommend this place for several reasons.
